The schools are connected by a chain, and the series history is recorded by adding brass "I" and "P" links to the handle after each game. picks.blurb: TCU vs Texas Tech Score Predictions From the KillerFrogs Staff Skip to main content SI.COM Frogs in the Pros FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM FROGS BB MEM'RIES SWEET TCU was unable to capture a win in its home finale against #2 Utah, losing 38-17. However, the Horned Frogs will get one more shot at becoming bowl-eligible on Thanksgiving Day against the No. 9-ranked Texas Tech Red Raiders. With Sonny Dykes no longer serving as the head coach of the Frogs, interim head coach Andy Avalos will be tasked with attempting to upset Texas Tech in Lubbock. Kickoff is set for 7 p.m. CT on ESPN. The Horned Frogs enter the game at 5-6 overall and 3-5 in the Big 12. Texas Tech is 10-1 and 7-1 in conference play. If TCU pulls off the big upset on Thursday, they will become bowl-eligible. Otherwise, the Frogs' season will be over. Either way, the Frogs will have changes coming their way. Texas Tech had a narrow win last week, as Baylor took the Red Raiders to the wire before they came out on top, 20-10. If the Frogs can make Texas Tech QB Thomas Castellanos uncomfortable like Baylor did, I like the Frogs' odds. Texas Tech has also struggled with consistency this season. However, the Frogs will have their hands full if they let him dictate where the ball goes. As I wrote in my Utah report card , the Frogs have quite a bit to fix, but I truly believe they will be playing hard for Andy Avalos in the regular-season finale. Can the Horned Frogs protect the football, play hard, and bring the energy? Here’s how the KillerFrogs staff sees the regular-season finale. KillerFrogs staff prediction standings through the Utah game, entering Texas Tech week. | KillerFrogs.com Why the Staff Picked TCU or Texas Tech Why the Staff Picked TCU or Texas Tech JD Andress sees Texas Tech’s defensive front posing a major problem for the Frogs, leaving the TCU offense without many answers. Michael Bara V believes the rivalry and the interim coaching change will bring out something special in the Frogs. He expects the defense to rally behind Andy Avalos and help TCU pull off the upset. Aiden Reed sees TCU eliminating Texas Tech from Big 12 contention, assuming BYU wins, as the Frogs take advantage of having nothing to lose and fighting for bowl eligibility. He also expects TCU to pull off its annual Thanksgiving upset. Baileigh Sheffield expects the Frogs to keep things competitive early, but sees Texas Tech pulling away in the second half for a two-touchdown victory. Jackson James is counting on history repeating itself, pointing to TCU's upset of an in-state rival after its last coaching change in 2021. He believes the Frogs will do it again on Thanksgiving Day in Lubbock. Skyler Gerard expects the Frogs to have some extra fire in their regular-season finale under interim head coach Andy Avalos. He’s counting on the defense to hold up as it has all season and help TCU pull off the upset. As for me, I have been saying all season long that the Frogs would upset Texas Tech, and I'm sticking to that prediction. I believe this team has one more fight left in it, and I expect TCU to rise to the occasion in Andy Avalos' first game as interim head coach. TCU (5-6, 3-5 Big 12) visit No. 9 Texas Tech (10-1, 7-1) in Week 13's Battle for the Saddle on Thursday, Nov. 26, at Jones AT&T Stadium in Lubbock, Texas (8 p.m. ET, ESPN). Kalshi lists Texas Tech as a 14.5-point favorite, with a total of 47.5 points and moneyline probabilities of 87% for Texas Tech and 16% for TCU. I'm fading the double-digit favorite in my latest college football picks . Spread prediction: TCU Horned Frogs +14.5 Total prediction: Under 47.5 Prop: TCU +3.5 first quarter TOP PICK TCU vs Texas Tech spread prediction: TCU +14.5 I'm fading the move toward the Texas Tech Red Raiders now that the spread has crossed a key number. I'll take TCU Horned Frogs +14.5, down to +12.5 . The Red Raiders opened as 10.5-point favorites at Kalshi. However, the line movement feels driven more by perception than new information . TCU firing Sonny Dykes this week is a new development, but Texas Tech's statistical edge and the Horned Frogs' absence of starting quarterback Jaden Craig were already factored into the opening line . More importantly, the Red Raiders rank 77th nationally in third-down conversion rate and 108th in red-zone scoring rate . That's a problem when laying nearly two touchdowns because converting in high-leverage situations is how favorites build a margin. TCU vs Texas Tech live odds movement TCU vs Texas Tech Over/Under pick: Under 47.5 The Under 47.5 is tradable down to 45.5 . Texas Tech can overwhelm TCU, so the Horned Frogs need to turn this game into a rock fight to have any shot at an upset. The Red Raiders have the 16th-highest rushing rate in the country, and TCU's defense ranks 18th in yards per rush allowed . Score prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Will Texas Tech football punch its Big 12 title ticket vs TCU? Score prediction Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The regular season comes to an end in Galaxy Stadium for the Texas Tech football team , with TCU coming to town for a Thanksgiving showdown under the lights. There's a lot going on here, but we'll begin with TCU, which will have a new coach running things and a new quarterback running the show. Well, not entirely new. Adam Schobel took the reins against Utah after starter Jaden Craig missed the game due to injury. TCU has already ruled Craig out for this week's game, so Schobel will take snaps and try to lead the upset over Texas Tech. The 6-foot-5 sophomore had one pass attempt this season before going 15-of-31 for 106 yards and throwing two interceptions against the Utes. But this game is less about matchups and more about what's on the line. What's at stake for Texas Tech football Things are pretty simple for the Red Raiders this week. Beat the Horned Frogs and they're heading back to AT&T Stadium on Dec. 4 for the Big 12 Conference championship game against Utah, which has already clinched a spot in the title encounter. A loss to TCU does two things. First, it makes Texas Tech wait another two days to figure out if it's heading to Arlington, needing BYU to lose to Cincinnati. Second, no win over TCU and no BYU loss means Tech can pretty much kiss its College Football Playoff chances goodbye. Speaking of the CFP, this could be an important factor in Tech's inclusion this year. Texas Tech currently has the one-loss appeal that could get them into the field as an at-large bid, likely on the road to start the bracket. Losing the game would wipe that possibility out entirely. Something to consider is that Texas Tech just getting to the Big 12 title game probably wouldn't keep them safe in the CFP field regardless of the outcome in Arlington. With the 12-team CFP field expiring this year, the committee doesn't have much reason to protect the participants of conference championship games, which are fading away after this season to make way for the 24-team playoff next year. Texas Tech's J'Koby Williams runs with the ball against Arizona State during a Big 12 Conference football game, Saturday, Oct. 17, 2026, at Galaxy Stadium. The fired coach theory and TCU TCU made the move to part ways with Sonny Dykes following the team's 38-17 loss to Utah. Things haven't worked out well in Fort Worth since Dykes took the Horned Frogs to the national championship game. Despite two nine-win seasons since then, TCU has lacked consistency in a Big 12 that's been gettable with some form of success the last few years. The question for TCU becomes: will it follow the trend of firing your coach and coming out the next game with your hair on fire? TCU is the fifth power-conference team to have parted with its head coach during the 2026 season, the others being Baylor, NC State, Maryland, and Florida State. Of those four other teams switching coaches in season, three of them won their next game, two of them (Baylor and NC State) earning wins of 21 points or more. This theory doesn't always come to fruition, however. During the 2025 coaching cycle, six power-conference programs fired coaches during the season and just one of them won their next game following the axing. That one win came from Virginia Tech, which beat Wofford, so it barely counts. Score prediction for Texas Tech football vs TCU Texas Tech 34, TCU 31: TCU's staff and players are all trying to impress whoever the next head coach is, so they'll be pulling out all the stops in this one. Texas Tech has to manage that, but the home crowd gets them back to Arlington. It might get there again soon, but for now, the rivalry is in a holding pattern. Florida is 20th in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after winning two straight to turn the season back around after a rough stretch. Florida State is waiting for new head coach Glenn Schumann to start, but the Georgia defensive coordinator is still a little busy for a bit at his current gig. He's on the way, but for now, the Seminoles can close the season strong with a win over the Gators and become bowl eligible. Florida State has played well under interim head coach Rick Stockstill, but when it had a chance for a sixth win and bowl eligibility, it lost to NC State 28-10 last week. It gets one more shot. The passing game is dangerous, but the Noles don't win when they bomb away. They win when they get things going on the ground, going 4-1 when running for 175 yards or more. It's possible to run on the Gators, but Florida State isn't Georgia, or even Missouri, when it comes to being able to grind. And then there's the other side. Florida is 7-0 when running for more than 120 yards. Run well on the Noles, beat the Noles. Why Florida State Will Win Everyone wants to win a rivalry game like this, and of course Florida will bring the full focus, but this is existential for the Seminoles. It'll be iffy whether or not the program would want to accept a bowl invite, or be able to, considering the regime change, but this is for six wins. This is for a bowl game. Florida's defense isn't bad, but it doesn't come up with enough third down stops. Florida State has to control the positive momentum from the start. It doesn't need big plays, but with its tempo, it has to keep the Gators on their heels with a good offensive balance. Florida vs Florida State Prediction, Betting Lines This should be fun. There's a new energy around the Florida State program, the team will come up with a strong first quarter, and then the Gator offense will start to take over. It might not start working right away, but Florida's offense will keep steadily producing. The flash might not be there, but it won't need to be. Kickoff is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. and will be televised on ABC. Florida State (5-6, 3-5 ACC) and Florida (7-4, 5-4 SEC) will meet for the 70th time, with Florida leading the all-time series 39-28-2, and winners of the last two matchups (40-21 in 2025 and 31-11 in 2024). FSU is 2-0 against the Gators on Fridays, winning 27-16 in 1979 and 45-38 in 2022, and the Noles have beaten five ranked SEC teams in the regular season since 2015, the most nationally among non-SEC programs. The Seminoles have started four running backs this season, including junior Zay Parks last week against NC State. Parks began his career as a walk-on and combined for 65 yards on 17 carries against Pitt and NC State, including a 9-yard touchdown on his first carry against the Wolfpack, FSU’s lone touchdown in the game. It was his second career touchdown. Meanwhile, on the Gators’ first possession Friday, running back Jadan Baugh will likely break the 1,000-yard mark for the season. Baugh already has 980 yards this season and averages 5.0 yards per carry. Baugh has recorded 8 explosive runs of 20+ yards, including runs of 75, 61, and 53 yards, and has scored 16 rushing TDs this season. UF’s Aaron Philo has firmly established himself as the starting quarterback after alternating with Tramell Jones Jr. earlier in the year. Philo enters on a two-game winning streak following victories over No. 11 Kentucky and Vanderbilt, where he completed 20 of 26 passes for 241 yards with no interceptions and added 73 rushing yards with two touchdowns. Receivers Bailey Stockton and Dallas Wilson are tied with 41 receptions each and a combined 5 receiving TDs. UF’s defense is led by linebacker Myles Graham, son of former NFL running back Earnest Graham, who leads the team with 88 tackles, 4.5 sacks, and 5.5 tackles for loss and returned a fumble 57 yards for a touchdown in last week’s win over Vanderbilt. Some other defensive players whose names we will hear mentioned are LB Aaron Chiles and DE Jayden Woods, who leads the team with 7 sacks and 11 tackles for loss. Last week against NC State, after marching 75 yards in 5 plays on their opening drive to score a touchdown, the Seminoles would only score a field goal in the second quarter, then were shut down and shut out in the second half. FSU was held to 283 total yards, lost the time-of-possession battle by over 13 minutes, and the defense gave up 464 total yards and almost 6 yards per play. Florida State shut out in the second half as Noles fall to NC State One of the few bright spots this season has been FSU kicker Gabe Panikowski, who is 27-for-27 on field goal attempts in his NCAA career, including 12-for-12 this season. He is the only active kicker (min. 15 attempts) in any NCAA division who is perfect in his career, and his 27 consecutive made field goals at the NCAA level is the longest active streak. Last week against NCST, Panikowski connected on a 54-yard field goal, the 7th-longest in FSU history. NoleThruandThru (season record: 8-3) As much as I’d love to see a win over those slimy lizards, I’m not going to be fooled again by FSU. At least we had an amazing kicker. An end to 2026 brings a glorious beginning to 2027 and beyond with a whoooooole lot of new faces on and off the field. Go Noles forever and forever and thanks for some fun memories, Stock! UF 31, FSU 20 Jacob Smith (season record: 6-5) It’s come down to this, yet again. This is the second year in a row that game number 12 will decide whether this team makes it to a low to mid-tier bowl game. Florida State’s defense is below average, while UF’s offense is above average. On the other hand, UF’s defense is below average, while FSU’s offense is above average. This could genuinely be the second-highest scoring game of the year. Though, I think UF takes it down the stretch because of all of the injuries on defense the Seminoles are dealing with. If I’m wrong, great! I look forward to playing in the Hot Sauce Bowl presented by Frank. Florida 48, FSU 35 Seminole Uprising (season record: 7-4) It is the dawn of a new day in Tallahassee with the hiring of Glenn Schumann this week. But, as the saying goes, it is always darkest before dawn. One last time, we have to experience the Mike Norvell era as the injury-riddled Seminoles take on Florida. Two weeks ago, after beating Pitt, I would have said FSU had a chance, but the NCSU game was so bad that it is hard to find the reasons why. Florida will run the ball down Florida State’s throats for the second year in a row, and the offense is not designed to play from behind or explosive enough to take advantage of the Gators’ coverage busts on the back end. For the second year in a row, the Seminoles go 5-7. UF 31, FSU 17 Jon Marchant (season record: 7-4 ) I think it’s safe to say the temporary bump from firing Mike Norvell has won off, and along with all of the injuries on offense this team is a shell of whatever it was earlier this season. The Norvell era wasn’t all bad but there was a lot of bad, and it never quite turned out the way we all wanted it too, Norvell included. I think they’ll play harder in this one similar to how they did vs Miami, but the injuries on offense will probably be too much to overcome. Again though, if there’s any takeaway from the Mike Norvell era it’s that any result, good or bad, was never off the table. Florida 31, FSU 23 Tim Scribble (season record: 7-4 ) I fear that this week’s game will be similar to last year’s result. The Florida State defense will be unable to stop UF running back Jadan Baugh. Expect a lot of yards on the ground for the Gators to officially close the Mike Norvell era. UF 35, FSU 20 Matt Minnick (season record: 7-4, ATS: 7-4) Man, I am so tired of losing rivalry games. I just don’t see how FSU will get UF off the field on third downs. And with so many injuries on offense, I don’t see how FSU will score beyond a random explosive play. The only way FSU hangs tough is by winning the turnover battle by a big margin, and that’s tough to do when your QB leads the country in INTs. UF 35, FSU 16 Curt Weiler (season record: 7-4, ATS: 3-8) Hard to shake my belief that this will be the third time in six years Florida denies FSU a bowl bid. The Gators haven’t been an incredible team all season but their highs have been much higher than Florida State’s. Florida 31, Florida State 20 Frank DNole (season record: 5-6) If you look at the Florida State vs. Florida head-to-head comparison chart above, you will notice that the Gators hold the statistical advantage over the Noles in almost every category. Normally, that might be the recipe for a Seminole defeat. However, this week we experienced a full moon that is now in the waning gibbous phase. Not only was it a full moon, but it was also a supermoon, and most importantly, it was a Full Beaver Moon (look it up). What all this means is that the Seminoles will win the offensive, defensive, and special-teams battles because the FSU players will give 115% more effort, they will want it more, and the Noles will play with more heart than their more talented turdly opponent. FSU Seminoles 34, FFFFF 31 P erry Kostidakis (season record: 6-5, 5-6 ATS) I really can’t tell you why I’m going with this choice other than pure delusion, but I have a weird feeling about this game. Here’s a fun fact: interim coaches have gone 3-1 in the series since 2017 (well, I guess technically 3-2, since the 2017 matchup was a matchup of two interims). Two of those wins were on the UF end, but if we’re talking delusion, why not warp some stats in favor of the home team? FSU has shed two streaks (last road win, last Friday win) that were defined by a win over the Gators this season since Rick Stockstill took over, so in the interest of the rule of threes, why not finally earn bowl eligibility with a season-ending victory over the boys from Hogtown? Again, this is a feeling borne out of nothing other than an inkling, since everything on paper and on film says UF should win this one with no issues. Jaden Baugh seems to take particular joy in the rivalry, which doesn’t bode well for an FSU defense that struggles against a lot, but especially against the run. FSU is stumbling in this health-wise, the high-flying feelings of go 2-0 to the Norvell era seemingly washed away by NC State. And unless Tre Wisner has made a turnaround on being healthy, Florida State is going to have to win this on the arm of Ashton Daniels, which the cope glass-half-full way of looking at it is that he has a penchant for performing in rivalry matchups. The only non-delusional, non-anything-can-happen-in-a-rivalry-game reasons I have for thinking that FSU is capable of pulling off a win is that 1) UF has played down to its opponents all season long and 2) the Gators are vulnerable on defense, especially through the air. But brother, it’s Turkey Day, and if there’s one thing I’m thankful for, it’s me never, ever, ever, ever, ever learning my lesson. We had to turn our antenna with a pair of channel locks to bring in one of three available channels. I came across this game, and being in love with football at that age, I kept the channel tuned. Of course, I noticed those gold helmets with the Spears on the side and immediately fell in love with Florida State. The Noles went on to win that game in Hogtown 37-9, and it was their first win in the series in a decade. I was hooked. By Ryan Potts in College Football Published: November 25, 2026 at 11:55 am EST Florida brings a powerful ground game into Tallahassee for the Sunshine Showdown. Florida State has dropped three of its last five and leans on a turnover-prone passing attack. See my specific spread pick and price below. The No. 20 Florida Gators travel to Tallahassee to face the Florida State Seminoles on Friday, November 27. Kickoff is set for 3:30 p.m. ET at Doak Campbell Stadium, and you can catch the broadcast on ABC. Florida brings a 7-4 record into this hostile environment after a gritty 34-27 win over Vanderbilt. On the other sideline, 5-6 Florida State is desperate to bounce back after a 28-10 loss to NC State. The ‘Noles need a win to secure bowl eligibility. I am looking past the emotion of the Sunshine Showdown and digging into the matchup numbers. Early Florida vs Florida State Prediction Florida wins by seven or more points. My early Florida vs Florida State prediction is a Gators win, and I expect them to win by more than a touchdown. Picking the winner and picking the cover are two different calls here, but I am backing the ranked Gators to put the final nail in the coffin for the Seminoles. Florida averages 31.6 points per game compared to 27.5 for Florida State. The Gators also allow fewer points, 26.3 per game against 26.6 for the Seminoles. The bigger edge is on the ground. Florida runs for 169.0 yards per game, and Florida State allows 171.0 rushing yards per game. That sets up Jadan Baugh perfectly. He has 980 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns, and a ground-and-pound attack lets Florida control the clock and keep the home crowd quiet. Baugh's Doak Walker Award pace has slowed considerably, but the junior still leads the SEC in rushing touchdowns and total touchdowns. With 20 rushing yards on Friday afternoon, Baugh would only be the third Gator (since 1956) with multiple 1,000-yard rushing seasons, joining Emmitt Smith and Errict Rhett. Baugh would be the only one in the group to do so in back-to-back seasons. Ball security is another focal point. Aaron Philo has thrown just five interceptions on 206 attempts, while Ashton Daniels has 14 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. away.headline: Florida shares injury update for star WR Vernell Brown III
away.blurb: Florida put out and official injury update on the star pass catcher Tuesday afternoon, saying that Brown has opted to undergo surgery on his injured knee. Per the statement, the procedure is expected to solve the lingering issue for good, but it will also keep him on the shelf for the “immediate future.” A 5-star recruit in the 2025 cycle, Brown became one of the biggest recruiting wins for the Gators in recent memory when he chose Florida over several other big name schools. He put together a solid freshman season under former head coach Billy Napier before breaking out during Florida's first 4 games of the 2026 campaign, becoming the primary target for quarterback Aaron Philo during that early stretch. He hauled in 17 catches for 271 yards and 2 touchdowns before suffering the aforementioned knee injury during the Gators' Week 4 win against Ole Miss, missing several weeks as a result. It initially looked like Brown would be able to return for Florida's matchup against Georgia , but he ended up reaggravating the injury during the bye week prolonged his absence. Resources MENU Home Jon Sumrall: Vernell Brown Ruled Out vs. Florida State Gators wide receiver Vernell Brown III has been ruled out ahead of Florida's regular-season finale against Florida State on Friday, coach Jon Sumrall said Monday night on Gator Talk. “He's had some consultations with some doctors on where he's at. He'll be out this week. He's not going to play,” Sumrall said. “He's dying to play. It's an unfortunate deal.” “It was substantial enough that we knew it would put him on the shelf for a little while,” Sumrall said. “Maybe a week, two, three weeks, didn't really know. But felt like there would be a timetable to return that wouldn't be terribly long.” Brown continued to reappear on the injury report in the weeks that followed. Coming out of the bye week, Sumrall said, Brown “practiced really good on Monday and Tuesday” before reinjuring his knee in a non-contact incident during Wednesday practice in Week 9, forcing him to miss Florida's matchup against Georgia. Before the Gators' 34-27 win against Vanderbilt on Saturday, Sumrall appeared unsure about Brown's return to the field. “It's hurting him as much as anybody. He wants to play. He cares. He's a Gator,” Sumrall said. “Can't wait to watch him get back on the field. He makes everyone around him better. He's a quarterback's best friend. You get him the ball in space and he makes things happen. But he will not be available this week.” Listen & Schedule Listen & Schedule The sophomore first appeared on the injury report after suffering a knee strain in the second quarter of Florida's Week 4 win against Ole Miss. Sumrall said the injury wasn't a ligament tear, but it was significant. “Wednesday he had a non-contact setback where he was just running a route down the field in our indoor facility,” Sumrall said. “And it tweaked on him.” The rivalry matchup against Florida State will mark the eighth game Brown has missed this season. “I'm hopeful he can play, yeah. away.blurb: – The biggest news from this week’s injury report is the status of EDGE Miles Capers. Capers was listed as probable in the middle of the week dealing with stingers. Vanderbilt head coach Clark Lea said Thursday that Capers has been doing okay overall and leaning on the side of precaution in practice. Last time out, Vanderbilt: Vanderbilt took its sixth loss of the season, dropping to No. 3 Alabama at home 21-6. Last time out, Florida: Florida got a big win on the road to become bowl eligible, beating No. 11 Kentucky 21-14. Vanderbilt Football at No. 24 Florida: Game Central Rundown, Injury Updates, TV Information Skip to main content SI.COM More from Vanderbilt Commodores FOOTBALL NASHVILLE — It is do or die today for Vanderbilt football. The Commodores currently hold a 4-6 record with two games to go before the end of the regular season. Vanderbilt must win both of the final two games to become eligible for a bowl game and earn a 13th game. The mission to do that begins today when Vanderbilt travels to Gainesville to play the Florida Gators in search of its second consecutive road victory. Two weeks ago, it went to Mississippi State and won 25-23. Today presents a different challenge. Vanderbilt knows its sense of urgency has to be at the highest it has been this fall. He'll be out this week. He's not going to play,” Sumrall said. “He's dying to play. It's an unfortunate deal.” “It was substantial enough that we knew it would put him on the shelf for a little while,” Sumrall said. “Maybe a week, two, three weeks, didn't really know. But felt like there would be a timetable to return that wouldn't be terribly long.” Brown continued to reappear on the injury report in the weeks that followed. Coming out of the bye week, Sumrall said, Brown “practiced really good on Monday and Tuesday” before reinjuring his knee in a non-contact incident during Wednesday practice in Week 9, forcing him to miss Florida's matchup against Georgia. Before the Gators' 34-27 win against Vanderbilt on Saturday, Sumrall appeared unsure about Brown's return to the field. “It's hurting him as much as anybody. He wants to play. He cares. He's a Gator,” Sumrall said. “Can't wait to watch him get back on the field. He makes everyone around him better. He's a quarterback's best friend. You get him the ball in space and he makes things happen. But he will not be available this week.” Listen & Schedule Listen & Schedule The sophomore first appeared on the injury report after suffering a knee strain in the second quarter of Florida's Week 4 win against Ole Miss. Sumrall said the injury wasn't a ligament tear, but it was significant. “Wednesday he had a non-contact setback where he was just running a route down the field in our indoor facility,” Sumrall said. “And it tweaked on him.” The rivalry matchup against Florida State will mark the eighth game Brown has missed this season. “I'm hopeful he can play, yeah. I'm hopeful everybody can play,” he said at the time. On Monday, Sumrall said Florida will take a patient approach. “I'm not going to push him back to play this year if it's not right,” Sumrall said. “It is something we want to make sure we get him fully healthy. home.headline: How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State
home.blurb: Florida hasn't lost to FSU since its horrific 5-7 season in 2023 when the Seminoles were a perfect 13-0 but still missed out on the College Football Playoffs. How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Rodgers officially a free agent How Brown's Season-Ending Injury Impacts Florida vs. Florida State (IMAGN Images via Reuters Connect) Jordon Lawrenz · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 25, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads As of Tuesday, Nov. 24, the Florida Gators officially shut down wide receiver Vernell Brown III for the rest of the season. This is news that came as no surprise , and it's crazy to see it take as long as it did. Brown had only suited up for four games this season, but he continued to appear on injury reports leading up to Florida's 34-27 win against Vanderbilt. The 7-4 Gators certainly could've used Brown in that brutal one-win stretch from Oct. 3 to Nov. 7, but at the end of the day they bounced back terrifically from Nov. 14 onward. Brown was a crucial part of this team's 4-0 start as he recorded 17 receptions for 271 yards with a pair of touchdowns. For reference, he's still third on the team in receiving yards, proving just how valuable he was during the few games when he was around. For the Gators, it's business as usual going into the final game of the year, a rivalry showdown at Florida State. Finally, Florida's offense knows it can move on once and for all without Brown. That's not a sentence they wanted to hear back on Sept. 26, but it's been a long time coming as his status had been in doubt for the better part of two months. Brown is only a sophomore, so the Gators risking further injury by putting him back on the field was never going to be the right answer. The Florida native made an immediate impact as a freshman with his 40 receptions for 512 yards. Obviously, this season took quite a turn with those losses to Missouri and South Carolina, and it doesn't feel like a coincidence that the offense scored fewer than 20 points in those games without Brown. Running back Jadan Baugh was not a factor in either of those games either, so that also didn't help the Gators chances when they lost their offensive superstar. When Brown and Baugh were both on the field, this team looked absolutely unstoppable. Now, it'll once again be up to Aaron Philo to keep this run-game going, though he looked much better through the air against the Commodores. Florida State enters this non-conference game at 5-6 overall, fighting for bowl eligibility against a Brown-less Gators offense.

By no means would it be a storied season that goes down in the record books, but it should be enough to keep Fickell from any more serious conversations about his job security. That being said, all that momentum would cease if Wisconsin were to lose to Minnesota, and knowing how inconsistent Wisconsin has been this season, there aren't many things you can bank on. However, we take our best cracks at three predictions below. No. 1: Wisconsin loses the turnover battle Wisconsin vs. Minnesota None of these predictions will come off as hot takes by any means, but perhaps this is the most levelheaded take on this list. On the season, the Badgers sit 80th in turnover margin at -2 against FBS competition. Minnesota, on the other hand, is 14th-best in the nation at a +7 margin. No. 2 Wisconsin's rushing offense is responsible for each of their touchdowns As previously mentioned, the Badgers are inconsistent this season, and usually when the offense looks like it has something figured out, the next week it falls apart. Well, last week the Badgers' offense ran for 381 yards across 51 total carries that involved two 100+ yard runners in Colton Joseph and Darrion Dupree. That being said, Minnesota's pass defense against FBS competition ranks 35th-best in the country, allowing 196.6 yards through the air. Their rushing defense, meanwhile, sits No. 74 in the country at 154.4 yards. If Wisconsin's offense is productive, it likely comes on the ground. No. 3 The two teams do not combine for 600 yards of total offense All that needs to be said here is that the Badgers and the Gophers each have a top-50 defense against FBS competition (Wisconsin 5th, Minnesota 42nd) while also posting total offenses that rank 118th and 131st. The Badgers have lost two straight Axe games; Wisconsin fans have grown discontent with the Luke Fickell era, and this win may matter more than any other win in his tenure. Fickell may not be able to keep his job if he loses this one. If Wisconsin does lose and he also keeps his job, there may be a riot in Madison. However, if he wins it, that changes things. Yes, there will still be a lot to prove and many unhappy fans, but this win goes further than maybe anyone realizes. It's a spread that continues to swing towards the Badgers for a few reasons. First, Wisconsin has had a better season, with a win over Purdue in their most recent game. That same Purdue team beat Minnesota. You could flip it and say Minnesota beat Iowa, who beat Wisconsin. So it's a mess. Second, the Badgers get to play at home, and even during these down years under Fickell, beating Wisconsin in Camp Randall is still hard to do. Wisconsin vs. Minnesota game prediction All that being said, let's make a prediction and see how close we can get to it. Last week, we predicted that the Badgers would beat Purdue 34-17. The final score was 42-10. Gave the Boilermakers too much credit and Wisconsin not enough. First, let's get the Vegas score. Using the spread and the over/under, we can get to a score prediction that Vegas is assuming, and for this game it's 23-15 in favor of Wisconsin. That's a good place to start, even if it's a weird final score. I guess in this rivalry, any random score could happen. However, let's get to our own prediction. It feels like Fickell will know he needs to prove it, Wisconsin players know they need to get the axe, and this time it will actually happen. BoH prediction: Wisconsin wins 30-19. How do you feel about that final score? Does it feel too high? Too low? It's hard to predict the axe game, as anything could happen, but it feels like this is the direction my brain thinks it will go. picks.blurb: Predicting Final Score of Michigan Football vs. Ohio State Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS The Game. Michigan vs. Ohio State . Buckeyes vs. Wolverines . It's the best rivalry in all of football and it's here. But it's not the normal game. Neither team is doing anything special with its postseason plans. The Wolverines nor the Buckeyes are headed to the Big Ten title game, nor does either team have a spot in the playoff. Instead, both teams are bowl-eligible, and as bad as Michigan's season has been, a win over the Buckeyes and Ohio State will have the same record as the Wolverines this season— 7-5. But Michigan will have to play another good game in order to pull off back-to-back upsets after taking down UCLA last weekend in triple overtime. Here's how Michigan on SI sees the game going. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Michigan's defense can go into Columbus and win the game against Ohio State. The Wolverines' defense has kept them in every game this season, aside from a second-half blunder against Oregon. The problem is Michigan's offense. We've seen 11 games from this unit and nothing really gets better. Savion Hiter ran for over 100 yards in the last two games, so there are some silver lining. And Ohio State's defense hasn't been good in the last four games. But the Buckeyes will have the best player on the field in Jeremiah Smith, who will be hard to defend. This game is 100% winnable for Michigan, but I haven't seen enough from the Wolverines' offense to believe they can make enough plays to pull off another upset . Final score: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 Justice Steiner This is one of the least anticipated versions of ‘The Game’ we have seen in recent memory. Ohio State is on the decline since starting QB Julian Sayin went down with an injury. But it does feel like both coaches are fighting to keep their jobs. If Michigan wants to win, they need to contain Jeremiah Smith the best they can and get Savion Hiter going in the run game. Also, continuing to get the tight ends involved like they did last week will be big for the UofM offense, something they haven’t done most of the season. Although I believe Michigan has a chance and the game will be close, I don’t trust them to pick up the win on the road. The best unit on the field will be Michigan’s defense, but Michigan’s offense will also be the worst unit on the field. I think the overall balance of the Buckeyes will be too much for Michigan to handle in this one. If Ohio State is motivated, and I have no reason to believe they won't be, the Buckeyes could roll. Final score: Ohio State 16, Michigan 3 Jacob Westendorf Ohio State is not what they usually are at this point of the year. A trip to Columbus has resembled more of a death march prior to 2022. This Ohio State team is not as good as any of the iterations Michigan has played since then. The Wolverine defense is good enough to keep them in the game. Jay Hill says he has a plan for Jeremiah Smith. The plan only goes so far. At some point, Ohio State's playmakers will just make one too many plays against Michigan's defense The Wolverine offense, which was still bad last week, will struggle again as the season ends at 6-6 with a narrow Buckeye victory in Columbus. Jason B. Hirschhorn From a playoff perspective, Saturday's matchup between Michigan and Ohio State lacks juice. The Wolverines fell completely out of the playoff discourse back in October, and the Buckeyes did the same after losing three of their last four games. And yet, the 2026 edition of The Game holds tremendous stakes for both sides. With another loss, Ohio State will exceed its total from the last two years combined and tie for its most in a single season with a non-interim head coach since 2001. Such a result could cost Ryan Day his job. On the other side, Michigan needs a win to avoid finishing a non-truncated regular season with a non-winning record for the first time since the Brady Hoke era. If Kyle Whittingham has any hope of surviving 2026, he'll need the political capital that comes with a victory over the Wolverines' archrivals. If star players determine the outcome, the Buckeyes have the advantage. Superstar wideout and Heisman front-runner Jeremiah Smith provides instant offense, and even the best teams struggle to contain him. However, if the Wolverines' defense can fluster freshman quarterback Luke Fahey and come up with a key turnover or two à la Chris Bracy's acrobatic interception against UCLA, they have a chance. Ultimately, slowing down Smith long enough for Michigan's lackluster offense to capitalize on the other end seems too big of an ask. Urban Meyer’s Ohio State-Michigan prediction comes with a caveat that may concern Buckeyes fans
picks.blurb: Urban Meyer’s Ohio State-Michigan prediction comes with a caveat that may concern Buckeyes fans - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Urban Meyer is picking Ohio State to beat Michigan on Saturday, which will surprise nobody who remembers his 7-0 record against the Wolverines as the Buckeyes' head coach. He made the call while speaking on stage at an event, in video Adam King of 10TV posted Sunday, and the Ohio State team he picked arrives at The Game in a place it has rarely been. The Buckeyes are 7-4 after a 31-28 loss at Nebraska, their fourth defeat of the season and their third in four weeks, following losses at USC and at home to Oregon. Their College Football Playoff hopes are gone, and they are unranked in the Coaches Poll for the first time since 2011. Julian Sayin has been sidelined since hurting his right arm against Indiana on Oct. 17, which has left true freshman Luke Fahey at quarterback. Former Ohio State Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer salutes the fans chanting his name during the College Football Playoff quarterfinal against the Oregon Ducks at the Rose Bowl in Pasadena, Calif. on Jan. 1, 2025. Ohio State won 41-21. Michigan, at 6-5, comes in off the biggest win of Kyle Whittingham's first season. The Wolverines beat previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA 18-16 in triple overtime on Saturday, Whittingham's 67th birthday, when Bryce Underwood found Jalen Hoffman for the deciding two-point conversion. Where Meyer sees The Game being won "The roster's better for Ohio State, but the best unit right now playing is the Wolverine defense, and that concerns me a little bit. They really hammered UCLA. You gotta think the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible, they're last in the country. And so to still have decent numbers, only one team's scored over 21 points on them, Oregon. So that's a legit defense. On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football. That's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, the offensive line's not playing great, so I think this is gonna be a rock fight, a low-scoring game. I think whoever punches the hardest is gonna win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game, and I've got the Buckeyes," Meyer said. In early October, Meyer called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck." Hearing him now rank their defense above every unit Ohio State has is about as clear a measure as any of how far the Buckeyes have fallen in a month. Urban Meyer came to love star quarterback Braxton Miller (5) and the rest of the 2012 Buckeyes, and to this day does not understand why they were punished for NCAA violations committed by predecessors. His case for Ohio State rests almost entirely on Jeremiah Smith, and the Nebraska loss showed what that version of the offense looks like with Fahey running it. The freshman's best moment in Lincoln was a 67-yard touchdown to Smith down the field. If Michigan's defense is as good as Meyer says, the Buckeyes may not get many clean shots like that, and a 17-14 game decided by a handful of throws to one receiver is a thin margin for a team that has already lost four times. Ryan Day was asked after the Nebraska loss if he still had confidence in defensive coordinator Matt Patricia, and he steered the answer straight to Michigan. "We don't have a choice. We've got to get this thing together next week to go win this game," Day said . Michigan and Ohio State kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. Michigan's offensive futility should make it easy to go chalk with the Buckeyes . It averages the second-fewest points per game among Power 4 teams and has vacillated between starting Bryce Underwood and Tommy Carr at quarterback. But the Wolverines don't need to score much with a suffocating defense. They also have a bit of momentum after an upset of unbeaten UCLA last weekend. The vibes just seem better in Ann Arbor, which might matter the most with only bragging right at stake. Rob Oller, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 16 : I went back and forth on this one before deciding that Michigan's offense is simply too anemic to pull off a win in Ohio Stadium. The Wolverines rank 130th in first downs, 128th in passing yards and 99th in rushing yardage per game. On the flip side, UM's defense, ranked ninth nationally, is the most reliable piece on either team, so if the Wolverines can hold OSU to 14 points they have a great chance at winning in Columbus for a third straight time. It likely comes down to which team's head and heart are into a game where the only thing on the line is bragging rights. Brianna Mac Kay, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 21, Michigan 17 : Ohio State's offense with Luke Fahey at quarterback has shown flashes of promise, primarily before the defense put the Buckeyes in a deficit across the past four games. If the defense can keep Michigan under its season average of 18.3 points per game, which ranks 129th in the country, the offense should be able to put together enough momentum to finish the season with a win over the Wolverines. Dan Aulbach, Columbus Dispatch: Ohio State 17, Michigan 13 : We finally get to see what happens when a stoppable force meets a moveable object. On the one hand, Michigan has the same starting quarterback as last year's edition of the rivalry, but Bryce Underwood has severely underperformed his expectations. Michigan's offense is lethargic, but Ohio State's defense has allowed 30-plus points in three of its last four games. Michigan's defense is elite (ninth in scoring defense), but so is Jeremiah Smith . The Buckeyes proved earlier in the year they can play and win against a defense-first team in Iowa, so I'll reluctantly pick the Buckeyes. picks.blurb: Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Urban Meyer Makes Ohio State-Michigan Prediction That Buckeyes Fans Won’t Like Former Ohio State head coach Urban Meyer is concerned about the Buckeyes heading into their game against Michigan Getty Michael Gallagher · HEAVY Mon, November 23, 2026 at 8:25 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads ANN ARBOR, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 29: Bryce Underwood #19 of the Michigan Wolverines is pursued by Kenyatta Jackson Jr. #97 of the Ohio State Buckeyes during the fourth quarter at Michigan Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Ann Arbor, Michigan. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) Getty Ohio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey after losing his last two games Getty It's been a rough month for the Ohio State Buckeyes. Ohio State started 6-1 but has lost three of its last four games. The latest was Saturday's 31-28 loss at Nebraska, which officially knocked the Buckeyes out of the College Football Playoff race. All that's left now is "The Game" against the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Columbus. On paper, Ohio State has the better roster. Even former Buckeyes head coach Urban Meyer admits that. Meyer, who went 7-0 against Michigan during his time in Columbus, still picked Ohio State to win. However, it sounds like he wouldn't be all that surprised if Michigan ended up leaving Columbus with a win. Urban Meyer's 1 Major Michigan Concern GettyMichigan and Ohio State both head into the Big Game with serious question marks Meyer spoke on stage at an event in a video posted Sunday by 10TV Sports' Adam King, and he didn't sugarcoat where Ohio State stands. "The roster's better — Ohio State — but the best unit performing right now is the Wolverine defense. And that concerns me a little bit," Meyer said . "They really hammered UCLA. You got to think, the other side of the ball for the Wolverines is terrible — they're last in the country. And so, to still have decent numbers — only one team has over 21 points on them all year, and that was Oregon — that's a legit defense. "On offense, we got the best player in the country, maybe the best player to ever play college football — that's how good Jeremiah is. But we also have a backup quarterback, and the offensive line is not playing great. So, I think this is going to be a rock fight; a low-scoring game, and I think whoever punches the hardest is going to win the game. I expect it to be a 17-10, 17-14 game and I got the Buckeyes." The numbers back up Meyer's remarks. Michigan ranks 17th nationally in scoring defense (17.5 points per game) and ninth in total defense (278.3 yards per game). And Oregon, which beat Michigan 31-7, is the only team to score more than 21 points on the Wolverines all season. The Wolverines' defense was at its best last Saturday in an 18-16 triple-overtime upset of previously unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. Michigan held the Bruins to 187 yards through three quarters and finished with three forced turnovers and four sacks. Why Urban Meyer Expects a Rock Fight vs. Michigan GettyOhio State head coach Ryan Day is sticking with QB Luke Fahey The biggest reason for Meyer's worry is at quarterback. Starter Julian Sayin hurt his right (throwing) arm in Ohio State's 19-15 win over Indiana on Oct. 17, and he isn't expected back for Michigan. That leaves true freshman Luke Fahey under center. Fahey went 16 of 27 for 259 yards, two touchdowns, and an interception at Nebraska. But nearly all of that came early: He was 9 of 12 for 163 yards and two scores in the first half, then 7 of 15 for 96 yards after halftime. Jeremiah Smith did his part (six catches, 165 yards, two touchdowns), tying Terry Glenn's Ohio State single-season record with 17 receiving TDs. Meyer also didn't pull any punches when it came to the other side of the ball for Michigan. "That defense is legit, legit because that offense is pathetic up there. It's the worst offense in college football, yet they're in almost all the games," Meyer said . "Their defense, what they did to UCLA, was absolutely phenomenal. Our defense has been up-and-down a little bit, but their offense stinks. I see this being a very low-scoring game. This is Ohio State-Wolverine football. The toughest team is going to win this game." Michigan's offense isn't quite the worst in the country, but it's close. The Wolverines rank 131st nationally in scoring (18.3 points per game). It's quite a shift for Meyer, who reportedly called the 2026 Wolverines a "train wreck" in early October. The Buckeyes (7-4) and Wolverines (6-5) kick off at noon ET Saturday at Ohio Stadium on Fox. away.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood expected to be available vs. Ohio State amid injury concerns
away.blurb: Despite injury concerns following last week’s game against UCLA , Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood is expected to be available vs. Ohio State , according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel . He was listed as questionable on the initial availability report Wednesday evening. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham had previously announced Underwood as the starter before news broke of the lower-body injury he was dealing with out of the UCLA win. He then came in as questionable on Wednesday’s first availability report. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage However, it appears Underwood will be able to go in the rivalry matchup against Ohio State on Saturday afternoon. It would be his second career start against the Buckeyes after getting the nod for last year’s game in Ann Arbor. The two teams are due to release their second availability reports Thursday evening. Underwood began this season as Michigan’s starter before Whittingham announced a change to Tommy Carr . But in light of Jason Beck’s departure as offensive coordinator, the staff opened the job back up, Whittingham previously said. Both quarterbacks played for Michigan against Oregon, and Underwood then started last week against UCLA. He went 11-for-24 for 127 yards and a touchdown, and he also completed the game-winning two-point conversion in triple overtime. “Well, like I said, last week, I believe it was, he’s handled this as well as he could possibly handle it,” Whittingham told reporters this week. “The change in quarterback, being demoted to the number two guy. Attitude never wavered. Work ethic never wavered. Preparation never wavered. He was just all-in every single day. “And I talked to him way back when the change happened. I said, ‘In this day and age of college football, odds are that you’re going to get another chance this season.’ And sure enough, he got his chance on Saturday and did a good job running the offense.” Underwood entered this season with high expectations, as did the Michigan program after Whittingham’s hiring. But as he looked back on the up-and-down nature of the year, the former top recruit said he will be better for it in the long run. “I can say the way I took this season was more of a blessing,” Underwood told reporters postgame after Michigan’s win over UCLA. “I took this as lessons being learned and everything, and how to move forward from it. “The way you can show how to be a man is facing adversity and how you take it on. That’s been my main focus these past, what, four, three, five weeks, however long. But just facing adversity, and how can I recover from it?” As a whole this season, Bryce Underwood has thrown for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, to six interceptions, with a 54.5% completion percentage. He has also added two rushing touchdowns across nine appearances.

As for running back Jordan Marshall, who was a game-time decision against UCLA and has watched his role diminish in recent weeks, there’s hope that he will be available. “It’s going to be close, but we’re hoping to get him back this week,” Whittingham said. home.headline: Report: Michigan QB Bryce Underwood expected to be available vs. Ohio State amid injury concerns
home.blurb: Despite injury concerns following last week’s game against UCLA , Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood is expected to be available vs. Ohio State , according to ESPN’s Pete Thamel . He was listed as questionable on the initial availability report Wednesday evening. Michigan coach Kyle Whittingham had previously announced Underwood as the starter before news broke of the lower-body injury he was dealing with out of the UCLA win. He then came in as questionable on Wednesday’s first availability report. $39.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage However, it appears Underwood will be able to go in the rivalry matchup against Ohio State on Saturday afternoon. It would be his second career start against the Buckeyes after getting the nod for last year’s game in Ann Arbor. The two teams are due to release their second availability reports Thursday evening. Underwood began this season as Michigan’s starter before Whittingham announced a change to Tommy Carr . But in light of Jason Beck’s departure as offensive coordinator, the staff opened the job back up, Whittingham previously said. Both quarterbacks played for Michigan against Oregon, and Underwood then started last week against UCLA. He went 11-for-24 for 127 yards and a touchdown, and he also completed the game-winning two-point conversion in triple overtime. “Well, like I said, last week, I believe it was, he’s handled this as well as he could possibly handle it,” Whittingham told reporters this week. “The change in quarterback, being demoted to the number two guy. Attitude never wavered. Work ethic never wavered. Preparation never wavered. He was just all-in every single day. “And I talked to him way back when the change happened. I said, ‘In this day and age of college football, odds are that you’re going to get another chance this season.’ And sure enough, he got his chance on Saturday and did a good job running the offense.” Underwood entered this season with high expectations, as did the Michigan program after Whittingham’s hiring. But as he looked back on the up-and-down nature of the year, the former top recruit said he will be better for it in the long run. “I can say the way I took this season was more of a blessing,” Underwood told reporters postgame after Michigan’s win over UCLA. “I took this as lessons being learned and everything, and how to move forward from it. “The way you can show how to be a man is facing adversity and how you take it on. That’s been my main focus these past, what, four, three, five weeks, however long. But just facing adversity, and how can I recover from it?” As a whole this season, Bryce Underwood has thrown for 1,077 yards and six touchdowns, to six interceptions, with a 54.5% completion percentage. He has also added two rushing touchdowns across nine appearances.

home.blurb: The Ohio State Buckeyes and Michigan Wolverines both have plenty to sort through on the injury front ahead of Saturday's rivalry game. Wednesday night's injury report brought some bad news for Ohio State and questionable tags for several Michigan starters, and both teams have decisions to make on who can go. Ohio State will be without linebacker Christian Alliegro. He joins quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja’Kobi Jackson, who had already been ruled out for the Buckeyes. Along with the players who are out, cornerback Jay Timmons and right tackle Phillip Daniels are both listed as questionable. Timmons was spotted in a walking boot after the Buckeyes' Week 12 loss to Nebraska, per multiple reports. Alliegro also had to exit early against the Cornhuskers and was unable to return. With Alliegro out, Ohio State will lean more on Riley Pettijohn, TJ Alford, and Payton Pierce. That trio will be the top three at linebacker, with freshman Cincere Johnson serving as the fourth option. The Wolverines already know JJ Buchanan will be out. On top of that, starting quarterback Bryce Underwood, running back Jordan Marshall, wide receiver Andrew Marsh, and defensive end John Henry Daley are all questionable to play against Ohio State. Daley’s status stands out on the defensive side. He's Michigan's leading sack man with eight sacks this season, and his absence would take away a big piece of the Wolverines' pass rush. If Marsh isn't able to play, Michigan would be down its top two receivers with Buchanan already out. That would put a lot on the rest of the receiver room against the Buckeyes' secondary. Ohio State LB Christian Alliegro is out Saturday vs. Michigan. DB Jay Timmons is questionable. pic.twitter.com/2xyIddwg6I There's plenty that needs to be answered before Saturday. Ohio State has to figure out if Timmons can go, he’d be the biggest loss for the Buckeyes if he can’t. Michigan is waiting on the health of its quarterback, its No. 2 running back, a top receiver, and its best pass rusher. The final injury reports will go a long way in shaping how this rivalry game plays out to say the least. Does it really matter all that much on a national scale? Yeah, it's getting stronger thanks to the consistent success of head coach Jeff Brohm at Louisville, and with Will Stein turning Kentucky into a rising power. The Wildcats might have slipped out of the CFP Top 25, but they've been in the mix over the last several weeks. Louisville is currently No. 19, and it might be the best ACC team available in the bowl process. Louisville vs Kentucky: Quick Hits Louisville has won six straight since losing back-to-back ACC games in late September. The 30-27 loss to Wake Forest was the difference between playing for the ACC Championship and finishing third in the conference. Kentucky started 7-1 but lost three straight. It's a win a way from this being the program's best season since 2021. Louisville won 41-0 last year, but Kentucky is 5-2 in the last seven meetings. How To Watch Louisville vs Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 12:00 PM ET TV: ESPN2 Location: Kroger Field, Lexington, KY – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Louisville Will Win Kentucky has stopped scoring. The offense wasn't horrible in last week's 28-14 loss to Missouri, and the passing attack wasn't awful in the loss to Tennessee, but the ground attack was stuffed by Florida, and the three turnovers against both the Vols and Tigers were a killer. Louisville's offense has been solid over the second half of the season, but it's the attacking defense that's taking over games. The Cardinals have forced 13 turnovers over their six-game winning run. Why Kentucky Will Win The Wildcats have to start taking the ball away again. That was part of the puzzle when the team was rolling, with 18 takeaways in the first eight games. There has been just one over this last three-game losing streak. Start forcing mistakes again, and the overall production will follow. UK quarterback Kenny Minchey has to crank up the big plays. All three Louisville losses came when the defense got hit by a slew of deep shots – Wake Forest, NC State, and Ole Miss all averaged over nine yards per throw. Louisville vs Kentucky Prediction, Betting Lines Kentucky has the talent, coaching, and experience to pull this off after losing the last two years by a combined score of 82-14. It's far better this season, but Louisville is too sharp, with too good a running game to be slowed to a crawl. It'll be a good, entertaining game, but Kentucky won't be able to score enough – it's 0-4 when scoring fewer than 21. It takes 30 to beat the Cardinals as the rivalry enters a new phase. picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville picks, odds for Governor's Cup football game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Kentucky vs. Louisville picks, odds for Governor's Cup football game Alexis Cubit and Ryan Black, Louisville Courier Journal · The Courier Journal Fri, November 27, 2026 at 10:09 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads For the first time, the annual Governor's Cup rivalry football game will be a top-25 clash between Kentucky and Louisville . The No. 18 Cardinals continued to climb in the rankings thanks to six straight wins heading into the regular-season finale after a commanding win over Pitt. UofL's defense held the Panthers to a season-low 10 points , while Cards quarterback Lincoln Kienholz had a career-best five touchdowns in the 32-point triumph . In doing so, Kienholz joined Lamar Jackson as the only Cards quarterbacks to throw 20 or more touchdown passes and rush for 10 or more touchdowns in the same season. Kienholz enters the Governor's Cup with 20 TD passes and 11 scoring runs. Meanwhile, the No. 25 Wildcats have steadily dropped in the polls because of a three-game losing streak to end SEC play. In Will Stein's head coaching debut, the Cats started league action on a high note and appeared to be on their way to Atlanta for the SEC championship game. But UK was outscored by a combined 83-34 in consecutive losses to Tennessee, Florida and Missouri. Turnovers and empty red-zone trips spelled trouble for Kentucky in its most recent loss, a 28-14 defeat against the Tigers. But the squad is looking to salvage the season with a win over the rival Cardinals. Can Louisville make it three straight wins over Kentucky, or will the Wildcats spoil the regular-season finale for the Cards? Here's what The Courier Journal's college reporters and columnist think. Stream Louisville vs. Kentucky football Kentucky vs. Louisville odds, moneyline, over/under Odds courtesy of BetMGM, as of Friday, Nov. 27 . Moneyline: Louisville -140; Kentucky +115 Spread: Louisville by 2.5 Over/under: 54.5 Kentucky vs. Louisville scouting report Why Kentucky has an advantage: Comparing the teams side by side, the Cats have an edge statistically in several areas. But UK's most notable advantage is keeping laundry off the field. Kentucky ranks among the top two in the SEC (and the top 20 in the FBS) this season in both fewest total penalties and fewest penalty yards. Louisville is nowhere close to that in either department. With the Wildcats lacking upper hands elsewhere, their discipline is one area they should be able to hang their hat on this weekend. Why Louisville has an advantage: Louisville comes into the Governor's Cup with one of the most high-powered offenses in the country. The Cardinals are averaging 38.6 points, which ranks eighth among FBS programs, and 462.8 total yards of offense, 12th-most nationally. Kienholz is coming off one of his best games of the season after throwing a career-high five touchdown passes in a dominant win over Pitt. He also has a strong group of talented receivers around him and two explosive running backs beside him. But the Cards' six-game winning streak is equally due to their defense showing great improvement and getting pressure on opposing quarterbacks. Louisville's defense comes into the Week 13 contest averaging 4.3 sacks per game over the past three contests. That included a season-high six sacks against North Carolina two weeks ago. Kentucky vs. Louisville predictions, picks for college football Week 13 Louisville 30, Kentucky 27. A banged-up Kentucky team will put forth a valiant effort. The Cats will have the entire weight of a frenzied Kroger Field behind them. But the momentum that saw UK win six straight games and debut at No. 6 in the College Football Playoff ranking at one point this season has disappeared. The hosts lose a heartbreaker at home as the Cards notch their third consecutive win in the rivalry. Louisville 35, Kentucky 31. The Cardinals will secure a fourth consecutive nine-win season and increase their winning streak over the Wildcats after catching fire during the latter half of the season. A high-powered offense and much-improved defense will spell trouble for Will Stein and his stumbling Wildcats squad in Stein's first game on the other side of the Governor's Cup rivalry. Brooks Holton Louisville 31, Kentucky 27. It's pretty simple: The Cards have won six in a row entering the regular-season finale, while the Cats have dropped three straight. Give me the hotter team. Louisville 32, Kentucky 24. For as well as the Wildcats' season started, I still think the Cards have their number. A noon kick down the road with the streaks each team is riding now? Yeah, I'll take Louisville. Louisville 20, Kentucky 17. UofL comes into the game with a lot of momentum, but whenever it seems one-sided in this rivalry, the underdog usually shows a lot of fight. Carson Hilbert adds his name in rivalry lore with a last-second field goal to win it for the Cards. picks.headline: Louisville defense preview: Kentucky has to finish drives
picks.blurb: Louisville defense preview: Kentucky has to finish drives - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Story by Wildcats Wire Louisville defense preview: Kentucky has to finish drives Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 25, 2026 at 11:27 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football is in a must win scenario heading into the Governor's Cup against Louisville to avoid a winless November. Over this losing streak, the Wildcats offense has been the main issue, in my opinion. They have scored just 34 points over the last three weeks, they are averaging just 11 points per game. We previewed the explosive Louisville offense, so Kentucky will have to match them to win this football game. Louisville ranks 41st in the FBS, allowing 128 rushing yards per game. They have allowed 12 rushing touchdowns on the season and teams have averaged 3.5 yards per carry against them. Kentucky will likely be without starting running back CJ Baxter, who was injured against Missouri. This puts a ton of pressure on Jovantae Barnes and Jason Patterson to carry the workload in this game, and the Kentucky offensive line has to dominate the line of scrimmage to open up holes for them on the ground. The Cardinals run defense is the strength of their defense, but they are one of the worst teams in the FBS defending the passing game. Louisville ranks 121st in the FBS in pass defense, as they allow 243 passing yards per game. They are similar to Kentucky in the sense they live off creating turnovers, the Cardinals have 12 interceptions this season. Kentucky will have plenty of opportunities in the passing game, as the Cardinals are the worst pass defense the Wildcats have faced all season, statistically. I would expect another huge game from Kenny Darby and Willie Rodriguez, who have been the clear top two targets for the Cats all season. Louisville will struggle to find answers for those two players in this game, but it will come down to the rest of the group making plays. We need to see DJ Miller get more involved, he has been inconsistent this season but we have seen flashes. Kentucky needs another pass catcher to emerge so it is not all on the shoulders of Darby and Rodriguez. Kentucky will be able to move the football, but they have to finish drives. This led to a loss against Missouri, as the Wildcats only scored 14 points and one touchdown on the Tigers despite having seven trips to the red zone. This game will play out similar to the one we just watched if Kentucky fails to finish drives. Louisville is similar to Missouri, they have a big play offense that can create scoring opportunities regardless of where they are on the field. The biggest difference is the defenses, that is a great Missouri defense that Kentucky had success on last week. It should be a lot easier for the Wildcats to finish drives and capitalize on their scoring opportunities in this game. All eyes are on this Kentucky offense showing signs of life after a three game losing streak where they have struggled in multiple areas. Will Stein gets to face the team he played for in his first ever Governor's Cup as a head coach, and his offense finding success will be the key to the Wildcats bringing the trophy back to Lexington.
