picks.blurb: Kentucky vs. Louisville game glance, opening odds, and our early prediction | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 27, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball College Basketball Recruiting Kentucky Wildcats Football College Football Recruiting Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Kentucky Football Odds Kentucky Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Library Community Guidelines Media Resources Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Library Expand Community Guidelines Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Football Kentucky hopes to snap a three-game losing streak and avoid losing a third straight game to Louisville. After a great start to the season, with a 7-1 record heading into the bye week and November, Kentucky Football has now lost three straight games. The Wildcats have suffered losses to Tennessee on the road, Florida at home, and most recently Missouri on the road. Heading into the Missouri matchup, Kentucky was ranked No. 16 in the AP Top 25 Poll. However, after a 28-14 loss to the Tigers, the Wildcats have officially fallen out of the rankings. Many Kentucky fans expected the team to bounce back against Florida at home, especially with a sellout crowd at Kroger Field. Unfortunately, the Wildcats came up short on their final drive. Meanwhile, against Missouri, Kentucky had several opportunities to score more than 14 points but struggled to capitalize in the red zone. Sacks, turnovers, and turnovers on downs ultimately prevented the Wildcats from putting more points on the board. While the final three games of the season have not gone well, not many fans expected Kentucky to reach seven wins during Will Stein’s first year, especially considering the difficult schedule the Wildcats faced. Although some fans are disappointed with how the past few weeks have unfolded, many are still pleased with what Stein has accomplished during his first season. Stein has even described the year as successful, despite the possibility of losing to Louisville at home to close out the regular season. Hopefully, that will not be the case. Now, let’s get into the Louisville matchup, as they face off for the Governor’s Cup. Louisville Cardinals (8-3) Kentucky holds the all-time series lead against Louisville, 20-17, but the Wildcats have lost their last two matchups against the Cardinals. Last year, Louisville went on to win 41-0, shutting out Kentucky on the road. That result ultimately contributed to former head coach Mark Stoops being fired. In 2024, the Cardinals also defeated the Wildcats, winning 41-14 at Kroger Field in another disappointing performance for Kentucky. Before that, Kentucky won five straight games against Louisville. Now, Will Stein, who played at Louisville, is leading the Wildcats and will face his former team for the first time as Kentucky’s head coach. As for Louisville, the Cardinals got off to a rocky start, opening the season with a 2-3 record. However, they have since won six consecutive games and improved to 8-3 on the year. A major reason for Louisville’s early struggles was its defense, which had difficulty stopping opposing offenses. Meanwhile, the Cardinals’ offense continued to put up plenty of points, keeping them competitive in several games. Now, things have started to come together for head coach Jeff Brohm and his team. Louisville will look to win its third consecutive game against Kentucky and improve to 9-3 on the season. The Wildcats will certainly have their hands full, as Louisville averages 38.6 points per game, which ranks eighth in the country. The Cardinals also allow 23.4 points per game, ranking 55th nationally. Kentucky will need to find a way to slow down dual-threat quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, who has thrown for 2,739 yards while completing 67.5% of his passes. He has recorded 20 passing touchdowns and four interceptions while also contributing 392 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns on the ground. In total, Kienholz has accounted for 31 touchdowns this season, making him one of the biggest threats Kentucky will have to contain. Louisville also has two talented running backs, with Isaac Brown leading the way. Brown has recorded 120 carries for 834 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Cardinals also rely on Keyjuan Brown, who has totaled 96 carries for 672 yards and six touchdowns. At wide receiver, Louisville has several players who contribute to the passing game, but three have emerged as the team’s primary targets. Tre Richardson leads the group with 58 receptions for 822 receiving yards and five touchdowns. Lawayne McCoy has recorded 36 receptions for 640 yards and six touchdowns, while TreyShun Hurry has added 45 receptions for 542 yards and three touchdowns. As mentioned earlier, Louisville has not been particularly strong defensively this season, but there are a few players Kentucky will need to watch closely. Stanquan Clark leads the Cardinals in tackles with 77, making him one of the team’s most important defensive players. Kentucky will need to find ways to avoid him in space and prevent him from making plays. Defensive lineman Tyler Thompson is another player to watch, as he has recorded 6.5 of Louisville’s 32 sacks this season. That means he is responsible for roughly one-fifth of the team’s total sacks, making him a major threat along the defensive line. Kentucky will also need to take care of the football, as turnovers have become a major concern over the past three games. The Wildcats have committed turnovers in every game since their matchup against Tennessee. Kentucky recorded two fumbles and an interception against the Volunteers, one fumble against Florida, and one fumble along with two interceptions against Missouri. Those numbers are concerning, especially considering Kentucky had only five turnovers before that stretch, including three against Alabama and two against South Alabama. Louisville’s defense has recorded 12 interceptions this season, with defensive back Kaleb Beasley responsible for five of them. Kentucky will need to be especially careful when throwing in his direction. The Cardinals have also forced eight fumbles, meaning the Wildcats will need to protect the football and avoid giving Louisville any extra opportunities. If Kentucky hopes to pull off the upset, it will need to play a clean game, limit turnovers, and find a way to slow down Louisville’s explosive offense. How to watch Louisville Cardinals vs. Kentucky Wildcats Location: Kroger Field — Lexington, Kentucky Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 12:00 p.m. ET Online streaming: WatchESPN Radio: UK Sports Network Opening odds: FanDuel lists Kentucky as a +2.5-point underdog after the Wildcats were previously -1.5-point favorites. ESPN win probability: Kentucky has just a 35.6% chance of winning, according to ESPN . Our early prediction: Before the season started, I predicted Kentucky would win six games but lose to Louisville, believing Will Stein would have too much emotion coaching against his former team, where he once played. While Kentucky is currently on a three-game losing streak and sits at 7-4 on the season, Louisville has won six straight games and is now 8-3. Many believe all the momentum is on Louisville’s side, which makes complete sense, especially since several other outlets are now predicting the Cardinals to defeat Kentucky. The Wildcats will need to finish drives and find a way to slow down Louisville’s high-powered offense. Kentucky has shown throughout the season that it can do that at times, including during matchups against South Carolina and LSU. With all of that being said, I believe this game will mirror the 2023 matchup, when Kentucky escaped with a 38-31 victory on the road. Although this year’s game will be played at Kroger Field, I believe the Wildcats will pull off another victory in a high-scoring contest. Kentucky will close out the regular season with an 8-4 record, solidifying what I believe has been a magnificent first season under Stein. Final score: Kentucky 34, Louisville 27. picks.headline: How Kentucky football and No. 19 Louisville match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (68.1% completions, 2,448 yards, 15 touchdowns vs. four interceptions) threw one interception as UK went 7-1 in its first eight games. The Notre Dame transfer has been picked off three times, however, during the Wildcats’ current three-game losing skid. As UK played from behind in last week’s 28-14 loss at Missouri, Minchey, a 6-foot-2, 211-pound fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw a season-high 43 passes, completing 27 for 288 yards with no touchdowns and two picks. • The UK defense has struggled this season against the quarterback run game and Louisville’s Lincoln Kienholz (67.5% completions, 2,739 yards, 20 touchdowns, four interceptions; 392 rushing yards, 11 touchdowns) is a more-than-capable runner. A 6-2, 215-pound junior from Pierre, South Dakota, Kienholz ran for a net-81 yards in a 44-17 win over Georgia Tech and has rushed for a net-40 yards or more in six other games. A transfer from Ohio State, Kienholz also has five games in which he has thrown for 300 yards or more, including last week’s 42-10 strafing of Pittsburgh, when he passed for 309 yards and five touchdowns vs. one interception. Advantage : Louisville Running backs • Kentucky running backs had a rough go in the loss to Missouri. UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (610 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 13 catches, 91 yards, one TD) and backup Jason Patterson (504 yards, 5.8 yards a carry, three TDs) each left the Mizzou game early due to injuries. With Baxter and Patterson sidelined, Jovantae Barnes (347 yards, 5.1 yards a carry, three TDs) carried a season-high 16 times for 69 yards at Mizzou and scored UK’s only touchdown on a 2-yard run in the fourth quarter. Barnes also lost a fourth-quarter fumble at the Missouri 13-yard line. • Louisville’s Isaac Brown (834 rushing yards, 7 yards a carry, eight touchdowns; 19 catches, 177 yards, two touchdowns) missed last season’s Governor’s Cup rivalry game due to injury. As a freshman in 2024, Brown won the game’s Howard Schnellenberger MVP Award after carrying 26 times for 176 yards and two touchdowns in a 41-14 U of L rout of Kentucky at Kroger Field. Senior Keyjuan Brown (672 yards, 7 yards a carry, six TDs) has run for 50 yards or more in six straight games. Wide receivers • Kentucky freshman Kenny Darby (57 catches, 711 yards, three touchdowns) made eight receptions for a career-high 110 yards in the loss at Missouri. In so doing, the 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, moved past Barion Brown (50 receptions for 628 yards in 2022) to claim UK’s freshman record for most catches and receiving yards in a season. After missing UK’s 21-14 loss to Florida two weeks ago due to injury, senior Nic Anderson (22 catches, 242 yards, one TD) returned at Mizzou and caught two passes for 19 yards. • Louisville leading receiver Tre Richardson (58 catches, 822 yards, five touchdowns) has caught 28 passes in U of L’s past four games. A 5-10, 175-pound senior from Topeka, Kansas, Richardson had a massive game against Kentucky last season while playing for Vanderbilt. In Vandy’s 45-17 decimation of UK in Nashville, Richardson caught six passes for 159 yards and three touchdowns. TreyShun Hurry (45, 452, 3) and Lawayne McCoy (36, 640, six) are also productive. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (58 catches, 560 yards, three touchdowns) caught eight passes for 93 yards in the loss at Missouri. That moved the 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School past Jacob Tamme (56 catches in 2007) for the most receptions in a season by a 21st Century UK tight end. Second-year player Mikkel Skinner (13, 115, 1) caught three passes for 18 yards vs. Mizzou and rushed twice for six yards. • Louisville’s Jaleel Skinner (25 catches, 362 yards, four TDs) is a cousin of UK’s Mikkel Skinner. In U of L’s 41-0 rout of Kentucky last season, Jaleel Skinner caught two passes for 21 yards and a touchdown. Advantage : Kentucky Offensive line • Kentucky right tackle Malachi Wood was knocked out of the Missouri game with an injury. UK coach Will Stein said Monday that Wood’s status to play this week is “day to day.” If the ex-Madison Central standout cannot go, left guard Olaus Alinen will shift to right tackle and Jordan Knox will move into the vacated guard spot. • Louisville left tackle Lance Robinson was named Outland Trophy National Player of the Week after earning a 90 grade with three knockdown blocks in U of L’s 44-20 romp over Florida State on Oct. 9. In that game, Robinson started at right tackle, moved to left tackle and also played a series at center. Center Evan Wibberley , played last season for Kentucky after spending his first three college campaigns at Western Kentucky. Advantage : Even Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (43 tackles, six sacks, 10.5 tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) tied for the team high with seven stops and had 1.5 tackles for loss at Missouri. After having a QB sack in three straight games against Oklahoma, Vanderbilt and Tennessee, Humphrey-Grace has gone the past two games without a sack. Tackle Tavion Gadson (39 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveries) made six tackles vs. Mizzou. • Louisville right defensive end Clev Lubin (49 tackles, nine sacks, 10 tackles for loss, seven QB hurries, two forced fumbles) is a disruptor. The 6-3, 260-pound Lubin had two sacks vs. UK last season. At right end, former UK player Jerod Smith II has made 20 tackles with 1.5 sacks and 4.5 TFL. Tackle Demeco Kennedy (28 tackles, one sack, three TFL) is a Frederick Douglass High School product who played with UK nose guard Jamarrion Harkless at both Douglass and then Purdue. • With 87 stops, Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey is the second-leading tackler in the SEC. A 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player, Godfrey has made double-digit tackles in four games this year. SLB Sam Greene (34 tackles, 1.5 sacks, two forced fumbles, an interception) made six tackles at Mizzou. • Louisville MLB Stanquan Clark (team-high 77 tackles, 1.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, five pass breakups, 2 QB hurries) has three double-digit tackles games this season. WLB T.J. Capers (70 tackles, 1.5 sacks, four TFL, three PBU, four QB hurries) intercepted a pass in last week’s dismantling of Pitt. Capers made four tackles, two solo, vs. UK last year. Defensive backs • The Kentucky pass defense had a rough go at Missouri, giving up 314 passing yards and four touchdown throws. Cornerback Terhyon Nichols was credited with seven tackles, broke up two passes and intercepted one. Safeties Jordan Castell and Ty Bryant each have four interceptions but Castell has gone four games and Bryant three without a pick. • Louisville strong safety Kaleb Beasley is stacking his stat line. The 6-1, 200-pound third-year player from Nashville, has made 68 tackles, broken up eight passes and intercepted five. A transfer from Tennessee, Beasley had three tackles last season for UT in the Volunteers’ 56-34 win over UK at Kroger Field. Former Kentucky defensive back DJ Waller Jr. has made 17 tackles and broken up a pass. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui is 14 of 17 on field-goal tries with a long make of 52 yards. Murray State transfer Thomas O’Hara only punted twice at Missouri, but averaged a booming 56.5 yards a kick. On the season O’Hara is averaging 42.9 yards but has pinned opponents’ inside their 20-yard line only five times on 22 kicks. Punt returner Brock Coffman , a former Louisville player, is averaging 8.9 yards on 12 returns and had a 55-yard touchdown vs. LSU. • Louisville place-kicker Carson Hilbert is 14 of 20 on field-goal tries with a long make of 54 yards. Hilbert is 6 of 12 from outside 40 yards. Punter Niall Hayes is averaging 40.2 yards and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line only nine times on 38 kicks. Punt returner Jackson Voth is averaging 13.5 yards on 14 returns with a long of 68. Isaac Brown has averaged 23.8 yards on eight kickoff returns with a long of 71. Pat Kelsey delivers the Seth Trimble injury update Louisville needed ahead of Texas Tech
away.blurb: Last week in the Cardinals' sluggish win over Stetson, UofL was without their starting shooting guard, Seth Trimble. Leading up to the game, reports said Trimble would miss it with a “minor injury,” and they expected him to be available Tuesday for Louisville’s matchup with Texas Tech. After gaining eligibility through the “five-for-five rule,” Trimble was one of Kelsey’s biggest additions from the Transfer Portal. He has started in every game this year, except vs. Stetson, when he was out, and with Louisville looking to pull off the upset, the UNC transfer will have to be healthy. The good news is that Trimble sounds like he will play in this huge rank-vs-rank matchup, and he is trending toward a return. Pat Kelsey delivers the Seth Trimble injury update Louisville needed ahead of Texas Tech Skip to main content About Louisville basketball recruiting Thanksgiving week is here, which means Louisville basketball’s Players Era 16 run is about to start. The Cardinals are currently in Las Vegas, where they are scheduled to tip off Tuesday, Nov. 24, for their first matchup of the event. Pat Kelsey challenges Flory Bidunga to become a centerpiece of Louisville's offense The Cards will look to secure their first marquee win of the season, as they face No. 9 Texas Tech. UofL enters this matchup 3-1, including their recent 83-69 win over Stetson. Pat Kelsey has struggled against ranked teams in the past, and tomorrow’s matchup will be a big test for this Lousiville squad. On Sunday, the Cardinals held a virtual press conference ahead of their game against Texas Tech, and Louisville fans got the Seth Trimble injury update they wanted. Seth Trimble is expected to play Tuesday against Texas Tech On Sunday, Kelsey confirmed the report is still accurate, as the Cardinals' head coach expects the UNC transfer to play. "Seth, we expect him to play," stated Kelsey. The Cardinals will need Trimble on Tuesday to pull off this upset, as the UNC transfer is a key piece to Kelsey’s offense and defense. He is a physical guard who will defend the opposing team’s best guard and will force turnovers, as he is averaging 1.7 steals per game, including two steals in each of the past two games. In addition to his defense, he is an offensive threat, averaging 13.3 points per game, the third-highest on the team, behind Flory Bidunga and Adrian Wooley. Trimble spent his first four seasons at North Carolina, including last season, when he averaged 14.0 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.0 assists, and 1.3 steals per game. The Cardinals have just a 29% chance of winning, according to ESPN Analytics, as the Red Raiders enter this game 5-0. Texas Tech already has a marquee win this season after the Red Raiders defeated No. 3 Illinois 84-78. Louisville and Texas Tech are set to play Tuesday, Nov. 24 at 8 p.m. ET inside Michelob ULTRA Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada. Home / Louisville Basketball About

home.headline: Kentucky vs. Missouri Injury Report: New injuries emerge for Wildcats
home.blurb: For Kentucky, four Wildcats were added to the injury report after not being previously listed this week. Punter Thomas O’Hara is now listed as questionable. Kentucky has been deploying both O’Hara and Wilson Berry at punter this season, though it was O’Hara who got the nod last week. Defensive tackle Ahmad Breaux has been added to the report, though he’s listed as probable, so there’s still a good chance he plays Saturday. Backup cornerback Isaiah McMillian is now on the injury report and listed as questionable. Fellow backup cornerback Kevis Thomas is now listed as out after not being previously on the report. Grant Grayton, another backup corner, remains listed as doubtful, so this could be a dangerously thin position heading into Saturday. For Missouri, the only change is that starting cornerback Jahlil Florence is now listed as probable after previously being questionable, so he should play Saturday. Everything else remained the same for the Tigers. home.blurb: Wildcats fans are hopeful Moreno will be available for Friday’s game against Wichita State, but his long-term health remains the priority as the season continues. With Moreno’s status still uncertain, Kentucky will need its other frontcourt players to step up if the sophomore center is unable to return against Wichita State. Mark Pope provides injury update on Kentucky big man Malachi Moreno | A Sea Of Blue Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Kentucky Wildcats Community A Sea Of Blue November 27, 2026 A Sea Of Blue Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Kentucky Wildcats Basketball FanDuel College Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Sections Expand Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Library Expand Community Guidelines Notifications Kentucky Wildcats Basketball Mark Pope said Malachi Moreno is responding well, after being in concussion protocol. For Kentucky Basketball , it feels like when it rains, it pours, and the struggles continue to pile up for the Wildcats. Kentucky has struggled against weaker opponents; along with that, it has suffered blowout losses against some of the better teams on its schedule. Now, the Wildcats could be without one of their most important players as they look to get the season back on track. On Sunday, Matt Jones of Kentucky Sports Radio reported that sophomore center Malachi Moreno had entered concussion protocol after an Indiana player dove on him during Kentucky’s loss to the Hoosiers. Moreno hit his head on the floor during the play and was unlikely to play in Friday’s matchup against Wichita State. Although Moreno remained in the game against Indiana, head coach Mark Pope provided an update on the sophomore big man during his radio show on Tuesday, explaining that Moreno began experiencing concussion symptoms on Saturday. “He’s doing good,” Pope said on his radio show. “He kind of got a whole 270 pounds landed on his head, and kind of started after the game, and then especially, really the next day, started showing some symptoms. “So we put him in concussion protocol, and he’s responded really, really well, and so we’re hopeful that he’ll be back sooner rather than later because he’s playing so well.” For Kentucky, losing Moreno for multiple games would be a significant setback, especially considering how productive he has been this season. The sophomore center is averaging 13.8 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists, 1.8 blocks, and 1.2 steals in 27.8 minutes per game. “He’s put up huge numbers, and he’s just playing at such a high level,” Pope continued. “It’s really important for us to get him back. picks.blurb: Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Clemson Given Lackluster Prediction Ahead of South Carolina Showdown (Ken Ruinard / USA Today Network / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images) Matt Levine · Roundtable Sports - Clemson Tue, November 24, 2026 at 11:55 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Clemson Tigers were able to take down the Duke Blue Devils on the road last week, picking up a massive win for the season. Clemson is now 7-4 on the season, with the team having won four of its last six games overall. The Tigers have rebounded nicely from a poor opening part of the season, despite a lackluster offense all year. But as the Tigers prepare for the final week of the regular season, the only focus is on getting a win over the rival South Carolina Gamecocks. Clemson will be hosting South Carolina in the game, giving themselves a slight edge entering the contest. South Carolina will come into the game with a record of 6-5 for the season, coming off two straight blow out losses. The Gamecocks have lost by a score of 34-6 in two straight weeks, and they will try to bounce back this week against Clemson. Both sides understand the rivalry aspect of this game, with the Tigers wanting to add another win to the season's resume. But South Carolina won't go down quietly, looking to spoil the Tigers' final home game of the year. Heading into the game, the Tigers are being viewed as the underdogs, despite having the better record than South Carolina. According to the ESPN matchup predictor , Clemson has a 44.2 percent chance of taking down the Gamecocks this week at home. Quarterback Trent Pearman will likely get the starting nod in this game after leading the Tigers to a win last week. Pearman did well enough for Clemson to win, and it seems that the program wants to see more from him in this game. Overall, Pearman went 17-of-27 for 164 yards, with no touchdown passes against the Blue Devils. But he did rush for 51 yards and a touchdown, showing that he can be a dual-threat option for Clemson. If Pearman can continue to help the offense, it could give Clemson an opportunity to grab the win. Clemson's defense has been strong all year, and South Carolina's offense has been very stagnant over the last few weeks. Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney has been criticized all season long , but if this team could get a win over the Gamecocks, it could go a long way for him. The 2026 season won't be seen as a complete success, but after how it started, the Tigers may end the year on a high note.

The former Clemson offensive lineman expects the Tigers to close the regular season with a second straight upset after winning 20-10 at Duke last Friday. "With all that said, Clemson is about to whip that ass," Mac Lain said. "I cannot wait to see this. The Tigers are going to win this thing." Fellow ACC analyst Kelly Gramlich also picked Clemson, though she sounded a little less certain about how this one plays out. The former Clemson football player came down with a late third-quarter interception against rivals South Carolina on Saturday night, ending a Gamecocks red-zone threat and helping top-ranked Georgia hold a 27-6 lead going into the fourth quarter. South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers was driving inside the Georgia 22 when he forced a throw into traffic. Barnes was lingering and waiting. The pick took away South Carolina's best chance to cut into the deficit and handed the ball straight back to the Bulldogs. It was the only turnover of the night for either team at that point and the only one South Carolina couldn't afford at the time. The Gamecocks, ranked 21st at 6-4, had managed just two field goals before the interception. Georgia, 9-1 and ranked first, had already built a two-score cushion behind two Nate Frazier rushing touchdowns and a pair of field goals from Peyton Woodring. For Clemson fans, the sight of Barnes snuffing out a South Carolina drive had to feel familiar probably even a tad bit confusing for the head to digest. He left Death Valley, but nobody let his instincts know that they should do the same. Somewhere in Upstate South Carolina, Tigers fans are watching a former player in a Bulldogs jersey do exactly what they would have asked of him, and deciding whether to be proud or just slightly annoyed that it's happening in another uniform. Barnes may be wearing a Georgia G now, but the Tiger paw is clearly still stamped somewhere in his blood. The Gamecocks will need to regroup quickly if they are to win this one. Georgia leads 27-6 with the fourth quarter just starting up. This was written in the fourth quarter of the Georgia vs. South Carolina game. away.blurb: WR Nitro Tuggle, DB Jalewis Soloman, WR Jayden Sellers, RB Matt Fuller, EDGE Kobby Sakyi-Prah, OL Josiah Thompson, OL Dayne Arnett and OL Seth Smith are all listed as out. WR Mazeo Bennett, EDGE Dylan Stewart, DB Judge Collier, WR Nyck Harbor and EDGE Anthony Addison are all listed as questionable. All five of those players are starters at their respective positions and would be a massive loss should they not play this weekend. What’s going on at QB? There was confusion galore around South Carolina’s quarterback room last week. Is LaNorris Sellers healthy? Would he be available? Is he going to play? What’s the definition of probable? Does anything anyone says really mean anything? The answer to those questions was that Cutter Woods started at quarterback for South Carolina in its loss to Arkansas. USC offensive coordinator Kendal Briles said “all” of the Gamecock quarterbacks practiced on Wednesday. It remains to be seen if Sellers will return from the ankle injury he sustained vs. Texas A&M or if Woods will get the second start of his career. Is all CFP hope lost? South Carolina’s hopes of making the College Football Playoff seemed completely lost after it was upset on the road by Arkansas last week. After all, there’s no way a team with four losses who was just defeated by an unranked team would stick around in the CFP rankings…right? Wrong. South Carolina remained in the CFP Top 25 , only dropping from No. 17 to No. 21. The odds of making the playoff are very slim but should South Carolina find a way to win out by beating No. 1 Georgia and Clemson then there’s a world where its playoff odds may graduate to just slim . Shane Beamer and the No. 21 Gamecocks will face No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. The game will kick off at 7:30 p.m. and be televised nationally on ABC. South Carolina (6-4, 4-4 SEC) is coming off a loss to Arkansas last week. Meanwhile, Georgia (9-1, 7-1 SEC) is coming off a win over Missouri at home. Georgia leads the all-time series over South Carolina 55-19-2. The Bulldogs have won the last four games in the series, including the last matchup in 2023. South Carolina’s last win in the series came in upset fashion in 2019. The Gamecocks haven’t beat Georgia at home in Columbia since 2014. Here’s everything you need to know about Saturday’s game. USC vs UCLA is a big deal because … 1) It's a battle between two top-15 teams in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. 2) A loss for USC would be devastating and could lead to a whole lot of changes, because … 3) UCLA is No. 9 with a 10-1 record, winning this game might be the only thing that gives the Big Ten a chance at getting two teams into the CFP. 4) It's USC vs UCLA. It might not be Ohio State-Michigan or Auburn-Alabama, but it's a big deal made bigger by the emergence of the Bruins. Back to the key part of all that. If UCLA wins, it's in the Big Ten Championship. Even if it loses, it can get in if Nebraska beats Iowa, Indiana gets by Purdue, and Washington beats Oregon – but it gets messier than that. Get past all the implications. It's a big showdown, the optics on a November afternoon in LA will be gorgeous, and it should be a blast. USC vs UCLA: Quick Hits USC has alternated win-loss over the last four games, losing to Wisconsin and Indiana on the road, and beating Ohio State and Maryland at home. UCLA suffered its first loss of the season at Michigan last week. This is the second time it has started a season 10-1 since 1998. USC has won three of the last four in the series. Klatt's Week 13 Picks Published Nov. 26, 2026 9:37 a.m. ET share facebook x reddit link The Game. The Iron Bowl. The top-25 Battle of LA. It all comes down to rivalry week. The 13th and final week of the regular season is here, which means some of the sport's best rivalries go down this weekend. Will UCLA avenge its Week 12 loss to Michigan and take down No. 15 USC, spoiling Lincoln Riley's chances at a CFP bid? As for the SEC, a win for Texas over Texas A&M and Alabama over Auburn will seal both teams' playoff paths. Additionally, is a win over No. 24 Washington enough to sneak Oregon into the playoff? Can Michigan carry its upset over UCLA into its road contest at Ohio State? For Joel Klatt , this weekend means everything. Here are Klatt's Week 13 picks and previews: Michigan vs. Ohio State: Preview Can Bryce Underwood lead the Wolverines to a road win at Ohio State? (Photo by Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: Ohio State -10.5 Moneyline: Ohio State -425, Michigan +330 Klatt's thoughts: "This game means everything to these fan bases. I think if you ask both of these coaches, they would tell you they know that, regardless of how the season has gone, they have to win on Saturday. Obviously, it saves what has been a disappointing season for both of these programs. Michigan was clearly disappointing in Kyle Whittingham's first year, and Ohio State was the preseason No. 1 ranked team in the nation. Ryan Day had Jeremiah Smith coming back, and obviously so much success. Both of these teams have won national championships in the recent past, and now here they are sitting this week, playing this game, and it's the only way to save their seasons. So, while nothing is on the line, everything is on the line … So, Michigan, they have a first-year coach, but Ohio State, you've got to win every single game, and here Ohio State has four losses. This is the only way that Ryan Day and his staff can salvage this season, even a shred of this season. You might even be a Buckeye fan and say, 'No, there's no salvaging it. You just have to win it. You just can't lose it,' and that's the nature of this game. "Here's what I expect when it comes to the actual game. I expect a very close game … I think they're both pretty good football teams, and specifically for Michigan, nobody except for Oregon has been able to run away from them. Every single game has come down to the last two minutes. Every single one. So, without Julian Sayin, and with the way that Ohio State has played on the defensive side, the way that their offensive line has struggled during the course of this year, do we really think that this is going to be a blowout? I don't think this is going to be a blowout. Not in any way, shape, or form. I think this game comes down to the wire because every Michigan game has come down to the wire … Kyle Whittingham has said that it'll be Bryce Underwood, and obviously Luke Fahey for Ohio State. These two guys have to play clean because I don't know if there's going to be a ton of points. Michigan plays incredible defense, and Michigan plays really poorly on offense, and Ohio State is kind of in the middle of both of that because they're not world beaters right now on either side of the ball. "But [Jeremiah Smith] is the most threatening player that they've ever seen. Because at any moment, one missed assignment, one wrong coverage, even if you play it perfectly, even in a double team, he can still beat you. You saw that against Nebraska last week. Caught that touchdown right before the half, in the middle of a double team, and Luke Fahey has gotten more comfortable and more comfortable and more comfortable. So as good as Michigan's defense is, they're going to have to be on top of exactly where Jeremiah Smith is at all times. Will they be able to block that Michigan defensive line? I think that's an interesting question … John Henry Daly, he's an All-American caliber defensive end. Dominic Nichols, he's excellent at rushing the passer … Ohio State has really struggled on the offensive line, really struggled. And I think defensively, Michigan's strength is, yes, they can cover, but it's more so they don't have to cover for long because of the pass rush. It's what ultimately got them into a position to score points, go to overtime and beat UCLA … This game is my favorite game to call. I know the fan bases don't like each other, but I can tell you this right now: neither team can afford a loss in this game because it means everything. Everything." No. 15 USC vs. No. 9 UCLA UCLA vs. USC holds massive CFP implications, with UCLA hanging on and USC trying to sneak in. (Photo by Ric Tapia/Getty Images) Spread: USC -6.5 Moneyline: USC -250, UCLA +205 Klatt's thoughts: "USC at UCLA. USC is a six and a half point favorite. We all know why: Ty Dieffenbach's injury … Now, when the X-rays were negative, I was like, 'Well, okay, now there's something,' because then it just comes down to like potential ligament, cartilage, soft tissue type of stuff, and then they have the MRI, and then Bob Chesney comes out, and he starts singing like, ‘Ty Dieffenbach might play. Ty Dieffenbach might play this Saturday.' No, no, no, not just he might play. He will play this season, and he might even play this Saturday. Now, is that gamesmanship for the committee? It didn't get penalized as badly as Indiana in Tuesday night's rankings. Is that gamesmanship for Lincoln Riley and USC? It might be, or is it the truth? Could we see Ty Dieffenbach on the field? That makes a huge difference in the way that you look at and preview and then pick this game, because obviously the spread is 6.5 against USC. "Why? Because we all saw Madden Iamaleava. I know that sounds harsh, but we saw him against Illinois, and then we saw him come in late against Michigan. I can just tell you this: I don't think that there's a third-string quarterback in the country that could have come in that situation with a game plan that was built for a different player facing Michigan's defense on the road. How do we get them outside the pocket? Maybe his skill set is different than Ty Dieffenbach, or maybe we might even see Ty Dieffenbach. Regardless of who's at quarterback, I think it's pretty apparent that UCLA is going to have to lean back into what was a strength for the better part of the year, but has not been great against some of the better teams, which is their run game. "So now you look at USC. Can they play defense the way that Oregon or Wisconsin or Illinois or Michigan play? I would actually say that their defensive line is actually pretty good. They might not be like the best defensive line in the conference, but they're pretty good. You look at guys like Luke Wafle, the true freshman, Jahkeem Stewart, Jide Abasiri. These guys can play. They've got some length, athleticism, some beef. And again, if you can't run it very well, and then all of that pressure finds itself onto the quarterback, that's advantageous for USC. I do think, though, for UCLA, the recipe to getting this win is takeaways. It's the short field. It's the way that Michigan was able to beat UCLA, and UCLA was not able to do that against Michigan. So the Bruins have to be advantageous … I do think USC is going to be able to scheme some things up for guys like Trent Mosley, Mark Bowman. I love those players; they're true freshmen, are some of the best in the country. "I just have a hard time picking UCLA with a third-string quarterback in this one … I like USC in the game, 24-17. I'll give the 6.5 and go with the Trojans." Klatt's straight-up pick: USC Klatt's pick against the spread: USC -6.5 Auburn vs. No. 6 Alabama Alabama opens up as 15.5 favorites at home vs. Auburn for the Iron Bowl. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Spread: Alabama -15.5 Moneyline: Alabama -700, Auburn +500 Klatt's thoughts: "Auburn at Alabama. The Iron Bowl. Alabama is favored by 15.5. That's a lot. It's the 91st edition of the Iron Bowl. This one's in Tuscaloosa. Keelon Russell got to rest last week … Auburn can get after it at the line of scrimmage. Here's the one area where you've got to be great in order to beat Alabama. You've got to rush the passer. Well, Auburn had six sacks against Arkansas and seven against Mississippi State. That was their last two SEC games. That's the path forward for them. I always think that spreads should not be this high. Alabama by 15.5 in a rivalry game is a lot. The one thing, well, there are a couple of things that I love about this Alabama team. Few things. One, Keelon Russell. Two, they're running it a lot better than they were a year ago. Last year, they were 128th in yards per carry from their running backs. "Alex Golesh. This is his first Iron Bowl. Obviously, Kalen DeBoer has been here and played in this game now. Byrum Brown, he got to rest, as well. He's pulled off some upsets in his career, namely, they beat No. 1 Georgia. But if you look at some of the other games against the more quality opponents in the SEC, I think that you can lay that more at the feet of Georgia didn't play well, rather than, 'Oh, this is in Auburn's bag.' So I think that Alabama will win this game. I know that they've been playing well as of late, but Alabama has the No. 1 rush defense in the SEC, and I think that this would have to be a heavy run game for Auburn in order to go out there and actually win. Alabama's defense is very good. I like Alabama at home, but it's a rivalry game, guys. Alright, and listen, I can't, I can't give 15 and a half. "I think Alabama wins it, 35-24, but I'll take the 15.5 towards Auburn." Klatt's straight-up pick: Alabama Klatt's pick against the spread: Auburn +15.5 No. 24 Washington vs. No. 12 Oregon Can the Ducks salvage their postseason path with a win over No. 24 Washington? (Photo by Jesse Beals/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) Spread: Oregon -14.5 Moneyline: Oregon -625, Washington +455 Klatt's thoughts: "How about Washington at Oregon? Oregon favored by 14.5. Oregon comes into this one knowing that a win will very likely get them into the Big 10 championship game. Of all the scenarios, like seven of the eight scenarios, Oregon wins and they're in. Okay, so they're playing for something. Meanwhile, Washington has a ton of confidence. They beat Indiana last week, and Demond Williams, when he's healthy and right, he is really good and dynamic as a runner. We all know that, and we all can see that. And I look up, and I'm thinking to myself, this probably is going to be a very good game. "Remember, Dan Lanning is only 2-3 against Washington in his career. Now, some of that was thanks to Kalen DeBoer and when he was at Washington, but it's not a great record in their rivalry game. What he has to lean on is that since they went to Jay Johnson, their offensive coordinator switch from Drew Mehringer to Jay Johnson, they went down against Northwestern, and then they came back from that. They've been sensational. In fact, if you look at Dylan Raiola, his last four games, nearly 300 yards per game throwing the football, 10 touchdowns, no turnovers. If he's playing like that, Oregon is very talented and should win this game at home. The defense has looked better. Remember, the defense is largely what allowed them to go on that 38-point run against Ohio State, and since then, they only allowed seven in each of their last two games, so they're playing a lot better. The one thing that I get nervous about Oregon's defense is that they let Drew Mestemaker and Aidan Chiles get loose a little bit, and now they're facing maybe the best one of them all in Demond Williams … I've seen it be tough for teams to follow up a big win like Washington had with another quality performance the very next week. We've seen that, but in a rivalry, I think

Can the Trojans put a dent in the Bruins’ faith – and their postseason hopes? Game 12: 'I Know the Score Like the Back of My Hand, Them Other Boys, I Don't Give a Damn' The USC Trojans (8-3, 5-3 Big Ten; No. 15 CFP Committee, Associated Press, and USA Today Coaches' Poll) close the regular season by visiting the UCLA Bruins (10-1, 7-1, No. 9 CFP Committee; No. 10 AP and coaches) on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 12:30 p.m. PST in Pasadena's Rose Bowl, and in front of a national CBS television audience. The Trojans are a 6.5-point favorite as of Thursday evening. This is the 96th Crosstown Showdown, with USC holding a 54-34-7 edge. The Trojans have won eight of the past 11 meetings, including last season's 29-10 victory at the Coliseum. USC also has won the past three Pasadena contests (2020, 2022, 2024). Last Saturday, the Trojans wrapped up their home schedule by topping Maryland , 35-21. USC scored 22 unanswered points in just over five minutes to turn a 14-13 third quarter deficit into a double-digit victory. Receiver Trent Mosley and running back Waymond Jordan each scored two touchdowns, and – a week after famously dropping four possible interceptions in a loss at Indiana – the USC defense snagged three picks to help flip the game on its head. The Bruins, on the other hand, saw their bid for a perfect regular season ruined in an 18-16 triple-overtime loss at Michigan. After UCLA tied the game at 10 with 10 seconds to play (on a fourth-down jump pass from running back Anthony Woods to tight end Brayden Loftin ), Bruin quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was injured on the first play of overtime and backup Madden Iamaleava struggled. The teams traded field goals in the first two overtime periods, then UCLA's two-point effort in the third overtime failed, before Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood hit tight end Jalen Hoffman to give the Wolverines the victory. Lincoln Riley (43-21 at USC; 98-31 in nine seasons overall) is seeking his fourth win in five tries against UCLA. On the other side, Bob Chesney (142-53 in 17 seasons as a college head coach) has seemingly transformed the UCLA program overnight, taking a club that was 8-16 in the prior two seasons and putting them just one win away from competing in the Big Ten Championship Game. Chesney is in just his third season at the FBS level (he went 21-6 at James Madison in 2024-25) but has brought a new energy and confidence to a program that hasn't played in a major bowl game in 28 years. Wayne Knight (Photo: Reuters - William Liang) Offensive coordinator Dean Kennedy has been with Chesney since 2022 (two years at Holy Cross and two at James Madison). The two are clearly aligned on a run-first style that is designed to grind on opponents both physically and mentally. It's a much-needed personality change for a program that's been perceived nationally for years as soft and disorganized. UCLA boasts the Big Ten's top rushing attack (194 yards per game, 22nd nationally), ranks 39th nationally in total offense (413.1 yards per game), and is tied for 42nd (with USC ) in scoring (30.9 points per game). Though the pass offense has been less reliable (219.1 yards per game is 12th in the conference and 78th nationally), it's provided a lot of big plays (UCLA's yards per completion – 13.77 – is 14th in the country). It has been good on third down (converting 44.5 percent, 30th nationally) but inefficient in the red zone (ranking next to last in the Big Ten). The Bruins also have been middling in pass protection (18 sacks allowed) and turned it over quite a bit (17 giveaways, 17th in the Big Ten). After starter Nico Iamaleava went down with a season-ending knee injury at Oregon on Oct. 10, Dieffenbach (a fourth-year junior transfer from Cal Poly ) kept the Bruins running steady. He's completed 59.6 percent of his passes for 1,406 yards with eight touchdowns and four interceptions. He's not a big runner (0.9 yards per on 46 carries). His injury last week seemed pretty brutal at the time, but the Bruin brass is saying he may play this weekend (which could also be a smoke screen, given how the College Football Playoff has treated possible playoff teams with injury issues in the past). He's been listed as questionable on the two official injury reports so far. If he can't go, the younger Iamaleava – a second-year freshman – is the expected pick. He has participated in three games, including last week's loss. He's completed 3-of-9 passes for 21 yards and has rushed six times for -3 yards. Senior James Madison transfer Wayne Knight has completely reinvigorated UCLA's rushing attack, ranking third in the Big Ten with 875 rushing yards and 5.6 yards per carry. He leads the conference with 13 rushing touchdowns and has 195 receiving yards on 24 grabs (two more scores). He scored in each of UCLA's first nine games, becoming the first Bruin to post non-passing touchdowns in that many consecutive games since 1953. He's ably backed by two seniors: Woods (5.8 yards per on 96 carries with six touchdowns; 10 catches, 55 yards) and Jaivian Thomas (66, 4.8, four touchdowns; five catches, 26 yards). The Bruin rushing attack has been quieter since Nico Iamaleava's injury, averaging 144.7 yards per game and less than 3.8 yards per carry in the last six contests. UCLA's receiving corps was completely refreshed in the transfer portal. Senior Michigan transfer Semaj Morgan is the leader (45 catches, 12.5 yards per, three scores). Sophomore South Carolina transfer Brian Rowe Jr. has 22 grabs (17.2, one touchdown), but fourth-year junior Florida transfer Aidan Mizell (18, 29.8, team-leading four touchdowns) has come on strong as a deep threat (he did suffer an injury late in the Michigan game but isn't listed on the injury report). Senior James Madison transfer Landon Ellis (10, 14.8, one touchdown) is the only other wideout with double-digit catches. The Bruins' top two tight ends are Loftin (10, 10.9, one touchdown), a senior Kansas State transfer, and Josh Phifer (six catches for 40 yards), a fourth-year junior transfer from James Madison. UCLA's offensive line has been roiled by injury during the second half of the season: after starting the same quintet in the first five contests, UCLA's used five different starting groups in the past six games. Senior South Alabama transfer Jordan Davis missed time at midseason but has been back in the lineup for the past two at left tackle. The drill's been similar for third-year sophomore left guard Eugene Brooks – back for the last two after starting the first six. It looks like fourth-year junior center Riley Robell (another James Madison transfer) is set to return this week after missing the last two with a lower-body injury. Senior James Madison transfer Carter Sweazie has started all 11 and returned to his preferred right guard spot last week after flexing around the line to cover some of those recent injuries. Senior Boise State transfer Hall Schmidt started the first nine at right tackle but has missed the past two and is out this weekend, as well. Senior Jaylan Jeffers has started the last two in his spot. Others who've seen time during the recent spate of injuries include third-year sophomore tackle Jensen Somerville , senior Eastern Michigan transfer tackle Mack Indestad , and senior interior linemen Julian Armella and Derek Osman (a Harvard transfer). Sammy Omoshigo (Photo: Reuters - Darren Yamashita, Reuters Connect) The story of UCLA's immediate rebound, though, has been on defense. Coordinator Colin Hitschler – who first worked with Chesney in 2011 at D-II Salve Regina before rejoining him at James Madison in 2025 – has UCLA playing an aggressive style that's paying huge dividends in havoc numbers. There are the 26 sacks, ranking 44th nationally – a huge leap from last season – but it's the takeaway numbers that are truly eye popping. UCLA has a nation-leading 20 interceptions and a Big Ten-leading 11 fumble recoveries (third nationally) – the total of 31 takeaways, of course, leads the country. But it's not a risk-heavy, all-or-nothing style: UCLA is sixth nationally in rush defense (88.5 yards per game), 13th nationally in pass defense (172.4, but first in pass efficiency defense), fifth in third-down defense (allowing a 29.6-percent conversion rate), and third in total defense (260.9). The Bruins are allowing just 14.5 points per game (eighth nationally). home.headline: UCLA's Ty Dieffenbach is latest example of confusing injury reports
home.blurb: On Monday, the national reporting on the health status of UCLA quarterback Ty Dieffenbach contained multiple contradictions. ESPN's Pete Thamel, for instance, wrote in a tweet that "Ty Dieffenbach isn't expected to be out long-term. While his status is uncertain for this week against USC, Dieffenbach is dealing with a minor hip injury. Dieffenbach is expected to be available for the College Football Playoff should UCLA clinch a bid." That piece of reporting veers in several different directions. When a player "isn't expected to be out long-term," that is generally viewed as news that an injury will be weeks instead of months or the full season. That does mean, however, that the injury carries short-term costs. If an injury isn't "long-term," it is short-term, so it exists. If an injury isn't short-term (meaning that the player is healthy enough to play his next game), there's no point or purpose in even saying whether the injury is long-term. Notice also how the reportage focuses on Ty Dieffenbach could be ready for the College Football Playoff in mid-December but also contains that oh-by-the-way part about maybe playing this week. All of this feels like a misdirection play, and it's understandable why UCLA might not be telling the exact truth. The Bruins have no incentive to do so, calling to mind the Florida State situation in 2023, when the Seminoles were left out of the playoff due to the injury to quarterback Jordan Travis. All of this aside, however, injury reports have become a source of confusion before this Dieffenbach situation at UCLA. USC football has featured plenty of situations in the Lincoln Riley era in which a player was abruptly announced as being out of a game when there were no outward indications of an injury absence during the week. Other players have been reported as having a chance to return on a given weekend only to miss that game and then multiple games after that, which meant that the original possibility of playing in Week X was never realistic. picks.headline: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri
picks.blurb: Week 13 college football betting, odds: 3 early bets to make right now, including in Oklahoma-Missouri - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Corbie Craig Contributing writer Tue, November 24, 2026 at 10:55 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College football rivalry week is here, and some of the toughest teams to price are the ones making changes this late in the season. Oklahoma has won three straight with Jason Witten calling plays, Minnesota just won after changing its offensive coordinator, and Wisconsin got a big performance from a quarterback who had lost his starting job. There are reasons to believe those offenses are improving, but I want to be careful about how much of last Saturday carries into this week. I'm starting with three unders, looking at the way these teams have been moving the ball and how much work it takes them to score. Here are my three early Week 13 bets. No. 19 Oklahoma at No. 24 Missouri (-1.5, 41.5) Oklahoma has looked better since Witten took over. Quarterback John Mateer has settled down, and the offense is giving its defense a chance to rest. I understand why people would expect more points here. Against Ole Miss, all three of Oklahoma's offensive scoring drives took at least 12 plays, and Isaiah Sategna added a punt-return touchdown, which helped turn a game in which Mateer threw for 111 yards into a 24-17 win. Then against Texas A&M, the Sooners were tied entering the fourth quarter before finishing a 15-play touchdown drive that took more than eight minutes. A later interception set up a one-play touchdown to Sategna, making the final score look a lot more comfortable than the game had been. Witten can keep Mateer in manageable situations, use the running game and keep Missouri's offense off the field. Oklahoma's defense has held Florida and Texas A&M to seven points apiece during this stretch, with Ole Miss scoring 17 between them. Missouri will test it. QB Austin Simmons threw four touchdown passes against Kentucky, and WR Donovan Olugbode caught two of them. I'm more concerned about those receivers creating quick scores than Missouri consistently driving the length of the field. The Tigers also allowed Kentucky into the red zone seven times while giving up only 14 points, so their defense gave up more chances than the final score suggests. I expect Oklahoma to stick with the patient approach that has worked under Witten, while making Simmons put together longer drives to score. Bet: Under 41.5 (-110) Minnesota at Wisconsin (-7.5, 37.5) Wisconsin just scored 42 points at Purdue, so this is a pretty low number to come back and bet under. RB Colton Joseph returned to the starting job and ran for 187 yards, including touchdowns from 32 and 66 yards out. Darrion Dupree broke a long touchdown run, too. Purdue couldn't handle the quarterback run game, and Wisconsin kept going back to it. Minnesota has to do a better job there. The Gophers allowed Northwestern to rush for 196 yards, and Joseph gave Wisconsin a way to turn a missed assignment into a touchdown without throwing the ball. That's the biggest concern with this bet — but I still don't trust Minnesota to score much. P.J. Fleck fired offensive coordinator Greg Harbaugh Jr. after the Penn State loss, and Eric Koehler took over the play-calling against Northwestern. Darius Taylor ran the ball better and two missed field goals hurt, but the Gophers still went into halftime scoreless. Their first touchdown required a fourth-down conversion, and Anthony Smith then forced and recovered a fumble to give Minnesota a short field for its second TD. QB Drake Lindsey made a great throw late to set up the winning field goal, but even with those plays, Minnesota finished with only 20 points. It hasn't scored more than that in any of its past six games. I can give the coaching change some credit without expecting everything to be fixed before a trip to Wisconsin. The Badgers' defense ranks No. 21 in our ratings, and neither offense is in much of a hurry between snaps. If Minnesota can make Joseph and Dupree string together first downs instead of breaking long runs, Wisconsin can move the ball while taking plenty of time off the clock. Bet: Under 37.5 (-110) North Dakota State (-9.5, 39.5) at San José State San José State nearly forced overtime against UNLV, but the offense still had to work awfully hard to get to 22 points. QB Luke Weaver threw 40 passes while the Spartans ran for just 56 yards. They needed a late touchdown pass to Carson Clark to get within a 2-point conversion then couldn't complete the tying attempt. A week earlier, they scored three points at Air Force. We still rank this offense 128th, and I'm not convinced Weaver gets enough help from the running game to keep it moving against North Dakota State. The Bison's defense certainly gave us a reason to hesitate last week. They led Northern Illinois 31-3 before allowing touchdowns on the Huskies' final three possessions. I still put more weight on a defense we rank No. 29, which held Hawai'i to 13 points and UTEP to seven in its previous two games. San José State needs to sustain drives against that group, and its past two games haven't given me much confidence it can. QB Nathan Hayes is coming off a career-high four touchdown passes, but the Bison finished Saturday by adding defensive tackles as blockers and handing the ball to DJ Scott to run out the clock. With North Dakota State favored here, I expect it to lean on the running game if it gets ahead. I'll back its defense to keep San José State from turning this into a game Hayes has to win through the air. Bet: Under 39.5 (+100)

away.blurb: Oklahoma vs. Texas A&M injury report: Who's out and who has to step up for the Sooners Skip to main content Recruiting OL Ryan Fodje: GAME-TIME DECISION Fodje injured his ankle in the loss to Kentucky and has been sidelined ever since. He was ruled out early in weeks until last week, when he was listed as doubtful before ultimately being unavailable against Ole Miss. He was questionable on Friday's report before becoming a game-time decision. Replacement: Although he's the starter at RG on the depth chart, Fodje could also replace E'Marion Harris at right tackle when he returns to the lineup. In the meantime, Heath Ozaeta has been anchoring that RG spot while Fodje has been out. Cornerback Dakoda Fields, who transferred from Oregon this offseason, has been out the last three games, and now, it's four after being listed as questionable until right before kickoff. RB Tory Blaylock: GAME-TIME DECISION Running back Tory Blaylock was also a game-time decision a week (and a day) ago before carrying the ball nine times for 48 yards, averaging 5.3 yards per carry. He's been a regular on the availability report after being banged up since before the season even kicked off, but he has still missed only the opener. He was listed as probable most of this week. Replacement: Freshman Jonathan Hatton Jr. will get touches whether Blaylock is available or not, but he should get even more if Blaylock is on the sidelines. We also had a brief Xavier Robinson sighting last week, so no Blaylock could help Robinson get on the field more. CB Dezz Ricks: game-time decision Everything seems to be going right for the Oklahoma Sooners right now, including a shrinking injury report. The No. 22 Sooners host Texas A&M on Saturday in Norman for a reunion between two old Big 12 rivals. OU, at 6-4, is eyeing a three-game winning streak and just appeared in the CFP rankings for the first time this season after back-to-back ranked wins. A lot of that newfound success is because of a change at offensive coordinator, with tight ends coach Jason Witten replacing Ben Arbuckle, but there's no doubt the Sooners getting healthier is also a major factor. It's not a long list, but there are still a few player statuses to keep an eye on before kickoff. This is the closest we've been in five weeks to seeing Ryan Fodje on the football field. If Fodje returns today, it would be the first time this season the Sooners have their full starting offensive line healthy. Before his injury, Fodje had started every game but the season opener, during which he was also injured. He's listed as the starter at right guard, but he hasn't actually played there yet this season. He filled in for Michael Fausi at left tackle for the five games he was healthy. The Ducks found their groove after getting down early against Ohio State, winning four straight, with the last three each by double-digits. Now they have a chance to play for the Big Ten Championship with a win. Win two more in a row, go to the College Football Playoff. Washington can screw that up, though. The Huskies picked a terrific time to play their best ball of the year, including wins at Purdue, Nebraska, and Michigan State before all but ruining Indiana's season last week in a 27-24 overtime thriller. Oregon is trying to close out its fourth straight regular season with at least a five-game winning streak. Oregon has won both games against Washington since the two programs joined the Big Ten. Washington's two wins over Oregon in 2023 won it the Pac-12 Championship on the way to playing for the national title. How To Watch Washington vs Oregon Date: Saturday, November 28, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: NBC Location: Autzen Stadium, Eugene, OR – Week 13 Schedule, Game Previews – CFP and Bowl Projections Why Washington Will Win The Huskies have been solid all year against the run, and there have only been a few meltdowns, but even when there's a little bending, there's not a lot of breaking. But the story has been the Dawgs trying to run the ball a bit more, and it meant everything against Indiana. This is hardly Army when it comes to the ground game, but quarterback Demond Williams Jr. took over against the Hoosiers, the offense made a point to grind it out a bit, and it set the tone early on against one of the nation's best run defenses. Yes, Oregon is playing well lately, but Michigan ran for 215 yards against the Duck D, Ohio State gave up on the ground and started winging it, and Michigan State was too battered to do anything right. Stay physical, and the Huskies can take control right away. Why Oregon Will Win Oregon is finally playing like a team that knows it's really good. The talent was there from the start of the season, but the Ducks were stunningly sleepy. Quarterback Dylan Raiola has settled in, and now he's playing with confidence. The throws are more decisive, the running game is sharper, and the turnovers that were a disaster in the loss to UCLA, and an issue in the middle of the season have slowed. The Ducks haven't turned it over in any of the last three games, and penalties aren't an issue. Basically, the team is playing better and sharper, and Washington usually needs takeaways. It didn't come up with any in the win over Indiana, but before that, the team was 5-0 when forcing multiple takeaways, and 1-4 when it didn't. Washington vs Oregon Prediction, Betting Lines Can Oregon avoid being overconfident? Everyone is putting it in the College Football Playoff, which not only assumes a win in the Big Ten Championship, but also a win over Washington to get there first. Can the Huskies be salty like they were against Indiana? Yes, and they're going to make it a much nastier fight than the coronation the Ducks might like. It'll be close throughout, but the Oregon pass rush will start taking over late in a terrific primetime battle (even if it's at the same time as Auburn vs Alabama). So, what are the experts saying about this game? Final Score Predictions for Oregon vs. Washington Oregon 24, Washington 18: Ryan Roberts, A to Z Notre Dame I expect this to be a physical, defensive-minded rivalry game where Washington makes Oregon work for everything early. Dylan Raiola could have a difficult start, with the Huskies doing a good job of making things uncomfortable and forcing him to settle into the game. However, I think Raiola will find his footing as the afternoon progresses. Oregon has too much offensive talent to stay quiet for four quarters, and I expect the Ducks to make the necessary adjustments to start moving the football more consistently. Washington will remain competitive, but Oregon’s ability to make plays in key situations will ultimately be the difference. The biggest difference in this matchup will be Oregon’s ground game, specifically running back Dierre Hill. I expect Hill to have a major impact, providing the Ducks with some much-needed offensive consistency while taking pressure off Raiola. His ability to create explosive plays and keep the offense ahead of the chains will be critical down the stretch. Washington will make this interesting into the fourth quarter, but Oregon’s balance offensively and ability to control the game on the ground will be enough to get it done. Oregon survives a tough rivalry test, taking down Washington 24-18. Oregon 37, Washington 20: Rob Gregson, A to Z Alabama This game suddenly has massive implications as the Oregon Ducks can make up ground in their chase for a College Football Playoff spot. But the game won't be easy. If you saw what happened last week between Washington and Indiana, the Huskies are out to play spoiler. The truth, however, is that the Ducks have been much better since making a change at OC, and quarterback Dylan Raiola has looked very comfortable. Washington let a bad Indiana team run up the score on them, and it almost cost them. This week, it will. Give me the ducks in a big one. Oregon 34, Washington 31: Tyler Forness, A to Z Florida Well, this game certainly got interesting over the last few weeks! It's already one of the nation's underrated rivalries, but after massive wins by both programs over Ohio State and Indiana, respectively, they are both riding high going into this matchup, and the Ducks somehow have a shot at making the College Football Playoff. This game could be the best one of the weekend, with Dylan Raiola and Demond Williams playing their best football of the season, and I think the Ducks get the last laugh. Oregon 34, Washington 23: Craig Smith, A to Z Tennessee The Ducks come into this contest riding a wave of momentum, having won four in a row including a statement 41-28 win over Ohio State in Columbus. The Huskies just made their own statement with a 27-24 overtime win over Indiana that put the Hoosiers between a rock and a hard place when it comes to the playoff rankings. Can the Huskies shake up the Big Ten for a second week in a row? Not in Autzen Stadium and not against this Ducks team. The Huskies have been playing competitive football lately, and I think that trend continues. But the big plays they gave up last week to Charlie Becker (six grabs for 167 yards and a 74-yard touchdown) are a sign of more big plays on Saturday by Dylan Raiola and his receivers. This one stays close on the scoreboard, but the Ducks remain in control throughout to do their part to earn a trip to the Big Ten Championship Game. home.headline: Washington Football WR Duo Questionable For Season Finale at Oregon
home.blurb: Both second-year players were listed as questionable on the Huskies' initial Big Ten availability report on Wednesday along with fourth-year defensive lineman Darin Conley, fourth-year edge Logan George, second-year edge rusher Devin Hyde, second-year kicker Hunter McKee and sixth-year running back Trey Cooley. Second-year offensive lineman John Mills is also listed on the injury report, though his availability at the midweek point is more favorable with a probable designation to play against the Ducks. Roebuck was also listed as questionable on last Wednesday's availability report ahead of UW's home finale against Indiana before being upgraded to probable on Thursday and Friday. The 5-foot-11, 190-pound sophomore went on to boast a career-high 10 catches in the Huskies' 27-24 overtime victory to go with a team-high 92 receiving yards, only the second time this season he finished with 90-plus yards in Big Ten play. Lawson and Conley made their first appearance on the availability report this season, both of whom, if ruled unable to go Saturday would deal a significant blow to the Huskies' odds of coming out of Eugene with the eighth win of the season for third-year coach Jedd Fisch. The other three players-Hyde, Cooley, and McKee-listed as questionable for the Huskies are each in a different spot with their injuries. McKee was a late addition and ultimate scratch last weekend while Hyde, who missed his first game at UW after appearing in 23 consecutive games, and the veteran Cooley have a chance to play but are completely up in the air for Saturday. As Fisch noted earlier this month, second-year running back Quaid Carr and third-year back Jordan Washington have been ruled out once again, with only Carr possibly able to return for the bowl game UW has already clinched with a 7-4 record going into the final game of the regular season. This article originally appeared on Huskies Wire: Washington Football WR Duo Questionable For Season Finale at Oregon Conley, a 6-foot-3, 290-pound transfer from Ball State, has come on strong over the past month for second-year defensive coordinator Ryan Walters dating back to UW's 38-26 road victory on October 16 against Purdue. Over the past five games, the defensive tackle has recorded 3 tackles for loss, all of which have been sacks with one each in back-to-back games at Michigan State and last Saturday against IU, becoming only the second defender to be credited with a full sack in consecutive games in the past two seasons since edge rusher Zach Durfee achieved the same feat last November at Wisconsin and against Purdue. George, a veteran transfer from Ohio State, appeared on UW's availability report for a third straight week despite playing in both of the past two games against the Spartans and Hoosiers, which should offer a glimmer of hope for Conley when it comes to projecting his availability in Saturday's rivalry game against the Ducks. Reporting by Lars Hanson, Huskies Wire / Huskies Wire USA TODAY Network

picks.headline: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12
picks.blurb: Four Bold Predictions for Oklahoma State Cowboys vs. Arizona State Sun Devils in Week 12 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football CFP And Bowl Games F1 Qatar GP 2026 – Practice 1 TRENDING Thanksgiving results: Bills slog past Chiefs Eagles rally past Cowboys Bears stun Lions Rodgers officially a free agent NBA Cup: Clinching scenarios Oklahoma State Cowboys head coach Eric Morris. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Matt Postins · Oklahoma State Cowboys On SI Fri, November 20, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Earlier this week Oklahoma State head coach Eric Morris made it clear his team has something to play for even with the Big 12 title game off the table. He didn't want to hear anything about lower intensity from his Cowboys (6-4, 4-3 in Big 12) as they prepared for a 9:15 p.m. central kickoff against Arizona State (6-4, 4-3) on Saturday. "[That's] such a silly question to ask - what is there left to play? For us, right now, it's building this thing up, and for our players that have fought so hard [finishing this season is important]." The Cowboys are bowl eligible for the first time since 2023. The Sun Devils are bowl eligible for the third year in a row. The winner of this game could end up with a better bowl bid with a victory. As the Cowboys prepare for a late kickoff against the Sun Devils, here are four bold predictions, including the final score. Caleb Hawkins Has 200+ Yards in Total Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys running back Caleb Hawkins. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Arizona State's defense has been better the past few weeks. It's part of the reason the Sun Devils have won three of their last four games. In that span, they've given up fewer than 17 points three times and allowed 27 points to BYU in the one loss. Arizona State has figured some things out and Morris noted that the Sun Devils have stopped the run well of late. The Cowboys have featured Caleb Hawkins in a big way the last five games. He's rushed for 648 yards and five touchdowns and caught 32 passes for 401 yards and three touchdowns. That's 1,049 all-purpose yards in five games. He's second in the country in the category. Oklahoma State wants to feature him. More important, given Drew Mestemaker's shoulder injury, the Cowboys NEED to feature him. He got 26 touches against Texas Tech and had 143 yards without a score. I suspect the Cowboys are going to feed him in the run game early to allow Mestemaker to settle in - I expected him to start - and then get him the ball in space in the pass game once Mestemaker is comfortably. The Cowboys need him to get 200 or more yards in total offense on Saturday. I think he gets it. Broderick Vehrs Plays a Role on Offense Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Broderick Vehrs. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As I just wrote, I expect Drew Mestemaker to start at quarterback. But it doesn't mean that head coach Eric Morris can't use Broderick Vehrs in some way. He's likely gotten some first-team reps this week on the off-chance that Mestemaker can't go. That has given Morris a chance to look at ways to use the true freshman in ways that could lessen Mestemaker's load and reduce his exposure to injury. Morris has gotten creative with the playbook at times. A couple of weeks ago he ran a play-action shovel pass that happened so quickly I'm not sure anyone realized it. There is little Morris can do if Mestemaker gets flushed out of the pocket. But he won't want to use Mestemaker in designed runs. That's where Vehrs can come in handy. He's shown an ability to run the ball in RPO looks that could help throw defenses off in the right circumstance. He has 58 yards rushing on just five carries so there is some explosiveness there. How Morris uses Vehrs will depend on comfort level. But a package that allows him a handful of plays to try and throw off Arizona State's defense would have the added benefit of minimizing Mestemaker's exposure to re-injury. The Cowboys Get a Defensive Touchdown OSU safety Evan Jackson. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect It's time. In fact, it's past time for the Oklahoma State Cowboys to land another defensive touchdown. It's Game 11. It's time for someone to find the end zone the same way safety Evan Jackson did against UCF. Why should the offense have all the fun? But why this week? The Sun Devils moved to true freshman quarterback Jake Fette as the starter three games ago and he's had a similar impact on Arizona State as veteran quarterback Thomas Castelllanos has had on Texas Tech. He's thrown for 623 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions. He's also rushed for 23 yards. He hasn't committed a turnover ... yet. Fette will be without one of his top wide receivers, Omarion Miller, who has caught 49 passes this season. He played last week against UCF, so Fette hasn't had the chance to play without the team's second-highest producing receiver. That takes away a rock-solid target. The Cowboys will also be looking for redemption defensively after giving up 52 points to the Red Raiders. Remember how Oklahoma State answered after giving up 51 points to Iowa State? The Cowboys allowed 28 points to Kansas State and forced three turnovers. That's the kind of bounce-back I'm expecting from the Cowboys this Saturday. That bounce-back will lead to a turnover that leads to a defensive touchdown. Given his hard work the past two months, I'll take the easy way out and say LaDainian Fields ends up with a pick-six. Score Prediction Oklahoma State Cowboys quarterback Drew Mestemaker. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Oklahoma State 37, Arizona State 33 The Cowboys haven't been great on the road this season. The performances have been uneven and they're 2-3 away from BPS. But Oklahoma State has followed up every loss with a win this season and I think that's what happens on Saturday. I think quarterback Drew Mestemaker plays without restrictions, but that running back Caleb Hawkins ends up being the star of the show. The defense frustrates ASU quarterback Jake Fette just enough to force him into his first significant mistakes of the season. Cowboys kicker Sam Keltner boots a career-long field goal in the thinner air of Tempe. After that, Oklahoma State will fly home for the regular-season finale against Kansas and awaits its bowl game invitation.
